content.p: Add:
Subdivision D—Determination in relation to action that is a component of a larger action

section.heading: Determination in relation to action that is a component of larger action

content.p: (1) A person who proposes to take an action (the larger action) may apply to the Minister for a determination that subsection 146D(2) does not apply to an action (the component action) that is a component of the larger action, if:
the component action is covered by an approval in force under section 146B of the taking of an action or a class of actions in accordance with an endorsed policy, plan or program; and
the larger action is not covered by the approval.
The application must:
be made in writing; and
be made in the approved form (if any); and
include the information or documents prescribed by the regulations (if any).

If the Minister is satisfied that it is appropriate for Parts 7 and 8 and paragraph 170A(c) to apply in relation to the larger action, the Minister may, in writing, determine that subsection 146D(2) does not apply to the component action.
If the Minister makes a determination, the determination takes effect on the day specified in the determination (which must not be earlier than the day it is made).
If the Minister makes a determination, the Minister must give the following persons a copy of the determination as soon as practicable:
the person proposing to take the larger action;
the holder of the approval;
the responsible person for the policy, plan or program.
If a determination is in force under subsection (3) in relation to a component action, the component action is taken not to be specified in the approval under section 146B.
Note: This also has the effect that there is no deemed approval under Part 9 of the component action (see paragraph 146D(1)(b)).

If the Minister decides not to make a determination, the Minister must, as soon as practicable, give the person proposing to take the larger action written notice of the Minister’s decision and the reasons for it.
A determination made under subsection (3) is not a legislative instrument.
Subdivision E—Exclusion determination

section.heading: Exclusion determination

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, determine that, despite an approval in force under section 146B in relation to actions in a class of actions, a specified action in the class that a person proposes to take is excluded, if the Minister is satisfied that:
the taking of the action has not substantially commenced; and
the taking of the action would result or be likely to result in an outcome; and
that outcome is in Australia’s national interest.
That outcome is the intended outcome for the national interest proposal that, under section 75A, the action is taken to be.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.
Despite subsection (1), the Minister must not determine that a specified action is excluded if the action is a fossil fuel action.
The Minister may make the determination:
if the person proposing to take the action agrees in writing—on the Minister’s initiative; or
on application under section 146Q.
The Minister must, as soon as practicable after making the determination:
give a copy of the determination to:
the person proposing to take the action; and
the holder of the approval under section 146B; and
the responsible person for the endorsed policy, plan or program to which the approval relates; and
the applicant (if different from the person mentioned in subparagraph (i)); and
publish a copy of the determination on the Department’s website.
The determination takes effect on the day specified in the determination (which must not be earlier than the day the determination is made).
A determination made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Application for exclusion determination

content.p: Any of the following persons may apply to the Minister for a determination under section 146P:
the person proposing to take the action as mentioned in subsection 146P(1);
if the person proposing to take the action agrees in writing:
another Minister; or
a Minister of a State or Territory.
The application must:
be made in writing; and
be made in the approved form (if any); and
include the information or documents prescribed by the regulations (if any).
The Minister must decide whether to make the determination, or refuse the application, within 20 business days of the day the application is made.
If the Minister decides to refuse the application, the Minister must give the applicant written notice of the Minister’s decision, and the reasons for it, as soon as practicable.

section.heading: Request for information

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, request any person to provide specified information that the Minister reasonably believes is necessary in order to make an informed decision whether or not to make a determination under section 146P.

If the Minister makes a request under subsection (1) in respect of a decision in which there is an applicant, a day is not to be counted as a business day for the purposes of subsection 146Q(3) if it is:
on or after the day the Minister requested the information; and
on or before the day the Minister receives the last of the information requested.

section.heading: Effect of exclusion determination

content.p: If a determination is in force under section 146P in relation to an action, then the action specified in the determination is taken not to be an action in the class of actions specified in the approval under section 146B.

Note: This means that no alternate pathway applies to the action under section 71A (because subsection 146D(2) does not apply in relation to the action), which in turn means that the action may be referred under Part 7 for assessment and approval under Parts 8 and 9.

section.heading: Revocation of exclusion determination

content.p: Revocation on request
The Minister must, by written instrument, revoke a determination under section 146P in relation to an action if:
the person proposing to take the action, or the designated proponent (if any), has made a written request for the revocation; and
the Minister has not decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133; and
the Minister has not made a decision under Division 2 of Part 7 that the action is not a controlled action.
Revocation on Minister’s initiative
The Minister must, on the Minister’s initiative, by written instrument, revoke a determination under section 146P in relation to an action if:
the Minister is no longer satisfied that the taking of the action would result or be likely to result in the intended outcome mentioned in subsection 146P(1); and
the Minister has not decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133; and
the Minister has not made a decision under Division 2 of Part 7 that the action is not a controlled action.
Timing
A revocation comes into force on the day specified in the revocation (which must not be earlier than the day the revocation is made).
Not legislative instrument
A revocation made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Notice of revocation of exclusion determination

content.p: As soon as practicable after revoking, under section 146T, a determination under section 146P in relation to an action, the Minister must:
give a copy of the revocation to:
the person proposing to take the action; and
the holder of the approval under section 146B; and
the responsible person for the policy, plan or program to which the approval relates; and
the designated proponent (if any); and
publish a copy of the revocation on the Department’s website.

section.heading: Effect of revocation of exclusion determination if Minister has decided action is a controlled action

content.p: At the time a determination under section 146P in relation to an action is revoked under section 146T, any determination that, under section 75A, was taken to have been made in relation to the action is also taken to be revoked.
Add:
Despite subsection (4):

any determination in force under section 79E at the time the request is made in relation to the action that is the subject of the original proposal continues in force, and section 79E continues to apply in relation to any such determination; and

any such determination continues to have effect for the purposes of sections 67, 67A and 74AA, and those sections continue to apply, in relation to the action that is the subject of the original proposal.
Add:

Note: Provisions of this Chapter that relate to section 79E (determination that certain reconsidered actions may continue to be taken) do not cease to apply in relation to the original proposal (see subsection 156A(5)).
Add:

Note: Provisions of this Chapter that relate to section 79E (determination that certain reconsidered actions may continue to be taken) do not cease to apply in relation to the original proposal (see subsection 156A(5)).
Insert:

section.heading: Determination that an action etc. is a national interest proposal

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, determine that the taking of a specified action is a national interest proposal if:
the Minister has decided, under subsection 75(1), that the action is a controlled action; and
the Minister has not decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133.
Note: The Minister is taken to have made a determination under this section in certain circumstances (see sections 75A, 75B and 75C).
Despite subsection (1), the Minister must not determine that the taking of a specified action is a national interest proposal if the action is a fossil fuel action.
The Minister may make the determination:
if the designated proponent of the action agrees in writing—on the Minister’s initiative; or
on application under section 157B.
Note: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 157G(1).
A determination made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Application for determination

content.p: (1) The following persons may apply to the Minister (the Environment Minister) for a determination that the taking of an action is a national interest proposal:
the designated proponent of the action;
if the designated proponent of the action agrees in writing—a Minister (other than the Environment Minister), or a Minister of a State or Territory.
The application must:
be in writing; and
include the information (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
The Minister must decide whether to make a determination under section 157A within 20 business days of receiving the application.

Note: If the Minister requests information to make an informed decision under section 157G, days between the request and receipt of the information do not count towards this timeframe (subsection 157G(3)).

If the Minister decides not to make the determination, the Minister must give the applicant written notice of the Minister’s decision, and the reasons for it, as soon as practicable after the decision is made.
Note: If the Minister makes the determination, the Minister must give the persons listed in subsection (1) a copy of the determination (see section 157D).

section.heading: Grounds for determination

content.p: Before determining that the taking of an action is a national interest proposal, the Minister must be satisfied that:
the taking of the action would result or be likely to result in an outcome; and
that outcome is in Australia’s national interest.
That outcome is the intended outcome for the national interest proposal.
In determining Australia’s national interest for the purposes of a provision listed in subsection (3), the Minister may consider:
Australia’s defence, security or strategic interests; or
Australia’s obligations under an agreement with one or more other countries.
This does not limit the matters the Minister may consider.
For the purposes of subsection (2), the following provisions are listed:
subsection (1) of this section;
paragraph 133(7B)(b) (non-disclosure of reasons);
paragraph 146P(1)(c) (exclusion determination for approval under section 146B);
paragraph 157D(2)(b) (non-disclosure of determination and reasons);
paragraph 157E(2)(a) (revocation of determination);
paragraph 157N(2)(b) (non-disclosure of exemption and reasons);
paragraph 157R(2)(b) (non-disclosure of variation and reasons);
paragraph 177BV(1)(b) (exemption for restricted actions);
paragraph 177BW(3)(b) (non-publication of application);
paragraph 177BX(4)(b) (non-publication of reasons);
paragraph 177CF(1)(c) (exclusion determination for priority actions under bioregional plan);
paragraph 302F(2)(b) (non-disclosure of exemption and reasons);
paragraph 302J(2)(b) (non-disclosure of variation and reasons).

section.heading: Notice of determination

content.p: As soon as practicable after making a determination under section 157A that the taking of an action is a national interest proposal, the Minister must:
give a copy of the determination to:
the designated proponent of the action; and
if a different person applied for the determination under subsection 157B(1)—that person (if any); and
publish a copy of the determination together with the Minister’s reasons for making the determination on the Department’s website.
However, the Minister must not publish under paragraph (1)(b) so much of the determination or reasons as:
is:
(i) an exempt document under section 47 of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (trade secrets etc.); or

a conditionally exempt document under section 47G of that Act (business documents) to which access would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest for the purposes of subsection 11A(5) of that Act; or
the Minister believes it is in Australia’s national interest not to provide.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.

section.heading: Revocation of determination

content.p: Revocation on request
The Minister must, by written instrument, revoke a determination under section 157A that the taking of an action is a national interest proposal, if:
the Minister has not decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133; and
the designated proponent of the action has made a written request for the revocation.
Note: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 157G(1).
Revocation on Minister’s initiative
The Minister may, on the Minister’s initiative, by written instrument, revoke a determination under section 157A that the taking of an action is a national interest proposal, if:
the Minister is no longer satisfied that the taking of the action would result or be likely to result in the intended outcome for the national interest proposal; and
the Minister has not decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133.
Note 1: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 157G(1).
Note 2: For paragraph (a), subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining the national interest.
Timing
A revocation comes into force on the day specified in the revocation (which must not be earlier than the day the revocation is made).
Not legislative instrument
A revocation made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Notice of revocation of determination

content.p: As soon as practicable after revoking, under section 157E, a determination that the taking of an action is a national interest proposal, the Minister must:
give a copy of the revocation to the designated proponent of the action; and
publish a copy of the revocation together with the Minister’s reasons for making the revocation on the Department’s website.
However, the Minister must not publish under paragraph (1)(b) so much of the revocation or reasons as:
is:
(i) an exempt document under section 47 of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (trade secrets etc.); or

a conditionally exempt document under section 47G of that Act (business documents) to which access would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest for the purposes of subsection 11A(5) of that Act; or
the Minister believes it is in Australia’s national interest not to provide.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.

section.heading: Minister may request further information for making decision

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, request any person to provide specified information if the Minister is satisfied that the information is reasonably necessary in order for the Minister to make an informed decision as to whether to:
make a determination under section 157A that the taking of an action is a national interest proposal; or
revoke, under section 157E, such a determination.

If the Minister has requested information under subsection (1) in respect of a decision for which there is an applicant, a day is not to be counted as a business day for the purposes of subsection 157B(3) (application for determination) if it is:
on or after the day the Minister requested the information; and
on or before the day on which the Minister receives the last of the information requested.
Repeal the Division, substitute:

section.heading: National interest exemption from provisions of Part 3 or this Chapter

content.p: (1) The Minister may, by written instrument, grant an exemption (a national interest exemption) for an action from a provision of Part 3 or this Chapter:
on the Minister’s initiative; or
on application under section 157K.
Note: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 157V(1).
To avoid doubt, the Minister may do so whether or not the action has been referred to the Minister under a provision of Part 7.
Content of exemption
The exemption must specify:
the action; and
each provision from which the action is exempt; and
the person to whom the exemption applies; and
the period for which the exemption is in force; and
any conditions imposed on the exemption under section 157M.
The Minister must be satisfied that the period specified for the purposes of paragraph (3)(d) is reasonably necessary to address the national interest that is the basis for the exemption.
When exemption comes into force
An exemption comes into force at the start of the period specified for the purposes of paragraph (3)(d) (which must not be earlier than the day the exemption is made).
Not a legislative instrument
An exemption made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Effect of national interest exemption

content.p: While a national interest exemption from a provision of Part 3 or this Chapter is in force for an action, the provision does not apply in relation to the taking of the action if:
the action is taken by the person to whom the exemption applies; and
the person takes the action in accordance with the conditions (if any) of the exemption.
Note 1: For conditions of an exemption, see section 157M.

Note 2: To the extent a defendant seeks to rely on this section as a defence to an offence, the defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this section: see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Application for national interest exemption

content.p: (1) The following may apply to the Minister (the Environment Minister) for a national interest exemption for an action:
the person who proposes to take the action;
the designated proponent of the action;
if a person mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b) agrees in writing—a Minister (other than the Environment Minister), or a Minister of a State or Territory.
The application must:
be in writing; and
specify the provision or provisions from which the person is applying for an exemption for the action.
Timeframe for decision
The Minister must decide whether to grant the exemption under section 157H within 20 business days of receiving the application.

Note: If the Minister requests information to make an informed decision under section 157V, days between the request and receipt of the information do not count towards this timeframe (subsection 157V(2)).
Notice if Minister decides not to grant exemption
If the Minister decides not to grant the exemption, the Minister must give the applicant written notice of the Minister’s decision as soon as practicable after the decision is made.
Note: If the Minister grants the exemption, the Minister must give each person to whom the exemption applies a copy of the exemption (see section 157N).

section.heading: Grounds for grant of national interest exemption

content.p: Before granting a national interest exemption for an action from a provision of Part 3 or this Chapter, the Minister must be satisfied that:
the action is, or is likely to be, a controlled action; and
for an exemption from a provision of Part 3—the provision is, or is likely to be, a controlling provision for the action; and
it is in the national interest that the provision not apply to the taking of the action by the person to whom the exemption is to apply.
In deciding whether the Minister is satisfied as required by paragraph (1)(a) or (b), the Minister:
if the action has been referred under a provision of Part 7—must have regard to the information provided in relation to the referral; and
whether or not the action has been referred under a provision of Part 7—may have regard to any other information the Minister considers relevant.
In determining the national interest for the purposes of a provision of this Division, the Minister may consider:
Australia’s defence or security; or
(b) a national emergency, including an emergency to which a national emergency declaration (within the meaning of the National Emergency Declaration Act 2020) relates.
This does not limit the matters the Minister may consider.
Note: The following provisions of this Division require the Minister to consider the national interest:
paragraph (1)(c) of this section;
subsection 157P(3);
paragraph 157S(1)(a).

section.heading: Conditions of national interest exemption

content.p: The Minister may impose one or more conditions on a national interest exemption for an action.
The Minister must be satisfied that any condition imposed is necessary or convenient for:
protecting, from the action, any matter protected by a provision of Part 3 that the Minister is satisfied is, or is likely to be, a controlling provision for the action; or

repairing or mitigating damage that has been, will be, or may be caused by the action on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3 that the Minister is satisfied is, or is likely to be, a controlling provision for the action.

section.heading: Notice of national interest exemption

content.p: As soon as practicable after granting a national interest exemption under section 157H, the Minister must:
give a copy of the exemption to:
the person to whom the exemption applies; and
if a different person applied for the exemption under subsection 157K(1)—that person; and
publish a copy of the exemption together with the Minister’s reasons for granting the exemption on the Department’s website.
However, the Minister must not publish under paragraph (1)(b) so much of the exemption or reasons as:
is:
(i) an exempt document under section 47 of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (trade secrets etc.); or

a conditionally exempt document under section 47G of that Act (business documents) to which access would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest for the purposes of subsection 11A(5) of that Act; or
the Minister believes it is in Australia’s national interest not to provide.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.

section.heading: Variation of national interest exemption

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, vary a national interest exemption:
on the Minister’s initiative; or
on application under section 157Q.
Note: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 157V(1).
The variation may vary any one or more of the following:
the specified action;
the provisions from which the action is exempt, but not in a way that results in the action being exempt from additional provisions;
the person to whom the exemption applies;
the period for which the exemption is in force;
the conditions of the exemption, including by imposing additional conditions.
Grounds for variation
The Minister must not vary the exemption as mentioned in paragraph (2)(a), (b) or (c) unless the Minister is satisfied that the exemption as varied is in the national interest.
Note: Subsection 157L(3) applies in relation to determining the national interest.

The Minister must not vary the exemption as mentioned in paragraph (2)(d) unless the Minister is satisfied that the variation is reasonably necessary to address the national interest that is the basis for the exemption as varied.

The Minister must not vary the exemption as mentioned in paragraph (2)(e) unless the Minister is satisfied that the conditions as varied are necessary or convenient for a purpose mentioned in subsection 157M(2).
When variation comes into force
A variation comes into force on the day specified in the variation (which must not be earlier than the day the variation is made).
Not a legislative instrument
A variation made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Application to vary national interest exemption

content.p: The following may apply to the Minister to vary a national interest exemption:
(a) the person to whom the exemption applies (the exempt person);
if a different person applied for the exemption under subsection 157K(1)—that person, with the agreement in writing of the exempt person.
The application must:
be in writing; and
specify the variation applied for.
Note: For the types of variations that may be made, see subsection 157P(2).
Timeframe for decision
The Minister must decide whether to vary the exemption under section 157P within 20 business days of receiving the application.

Note: If the Minister requests information to make an informed decision under section 157V, days between the request and receipt of the information do not count towards this timeframe (subsection 157V(2)).
Notice if Minister decides not to vary exemption
If the Minister decides not to vary the exemption, the Minister must give the applicant written notice of the Minister’s decision as soon as practicable after the decision is made.
Note: If the Minister varies the exemption, the Minister must give the applicant a copy of the variation (see section 157R).

section.heading: Notice of variation of national interest exemption

content.p: As soon as practicable after varying a national interest exemption under section 157P, the Minister must:
give a copy of the variation to:
the person to whom the exemption, as varied, applies; and
if a different person applied for the variation—that person; and
publish a copy of the variation together with the Minister’s reasons for varying the exemption on the Department’s website.
However, the Minister must not publish under paragraph (1)(b) so much of the variation or reasons as:
is:
(i) an exempt document under section 47 of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (trade secrets etc.); or

a conditionally exempt document under section 47G of that Act (business documents) to which access would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest for the purposes of subsection 11A(5) of that Act; or
the Minister believes it is in Australia’s national interest not to provide.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.

section.heading: Revocation of national interest exemption

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, revoke a national interest exemption, on the Minister’s initiative, if the Minister reasonably believes that:
the exemption is no longer in the national interest; or
a condition of the exemption has been contravened.
Note 1: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 157V(1).
Note 2: For paragraph (a), subsection 157L(3) applies in relation to determining the national interest.
Note 3: A national interest exemption is taken to be revoked if the Minister decides to accept the surrender of the exemption under section 157U.
A revocation comes into force on the day specified in the revocation (which must not be earlier than the day the revocation is made).
A revocation made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Notice of revocation of national interest exemption

content.p: As soon as practicable after revoking a national interest exemption under section 157S, the Minister must:
give a copy of the revocation to:
the person to whom the exemption applied immediately before the revocation; and
if a different person applied for the exemption under subsection 157K(1)—that person; and
publish a copy of the revocation together with the Minister’s reasons for revoking the exemption on the Department’s website.

section.heading: Surrender of national interest exemption

content.p: A person to whom a national interest exemption applies may, in writing, request the Minister to accept the surrender of the exemption.
The Minister must decide whether or not to accept the surrender within 20 business days of receiving the application.

Note: If the Minister requests information to make an informed decision under section 157V, days between the request and receipt of the information do not count towards this timeframe (subsection 157V(2)).
In deciding whether or not to accept the surrender, the Minister may have regard to any matter the Minister considers relevant.
Notice of decision
As soon as practicable after the decision is made, the Minister must:
give written notice of the decision to:
the person who made the request; and
if a different person applied for the exemption under subsection 157K(1)—that person; and
if the Minister decides to accept the surrender—publish the notice on the Department’s website.
Effect of surrender

If the Minister decides to accept the surrender, the exemption is taken to be revoked with effect from the day specified in the notice (which must not be earlier than the day the notice is published under paragraph (4)(b)).

section.heading: Minister may request further information for making decision

content.p: The Minister may request any of the following persons to provide specified information if the Minister is satisfied that the information is reasonably necessary in order for the Minister to make an informed decision as to whether to grant, vary, revoke or accept the surrender of a national interest exemption for an action:
the applicant for the decision (if any);
if there is no applicant—the person who proposes to take, is taking or has taken the action, or who is the designated proponent of the action;
in any case—the person to whom the exemption applies or is proposed to apply;
any other person the Minister considers appropriate.

If the Minister has requested information under subsection (1) in respect of a decision for which there is an applicant, a day is not to be counted as a business day for the purposes of subsection 157K(3) (application for exemption), 157Q(3) (application to vary exemption) or 157U(2) (application to surrender exemption) if it is:
on or after the day the Minister requested the information; and
on or before the day on which the Minister receives the last of the information requested.

Subdivision A—Duties in relation to certain authorisations

section.heading: Duties in relation to certain authorisations

content.p: The Commonwealth, or a Commonwealth agency, must not do a thing specified in subsection (2), if doing the thing, or a result of doing the thing, would be inconsistent with Australia’s international obligations under a designated international agreement.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the things are the following:

entering into a contract, agreement or arrangement, under Australia’s foreign aid program, for the implementation of a project that has, will have or is likely to have a significant impact on the environment anywhere in the world;
a prescribed activity.

section.heading: Seeking the Minister’s advice

content.p: (1) The Minister administering the Airports Act 1996 (the Transport Minister) may request the advice of the Minister administering this Act in relation to an authorisation relating to the adoption or implementation of a major development plan (within the meaning of that Act), including a variation or renewal of such an authorisation.
If the Minister administering this Act receives a request for advice under subsection (1), the Minister must either:

provide advice to the Transport Minister that the requested advice is not required.

section.heading: Advanced restoration actions

content.p: (1) The regulations may make provision for and in relation to advanced restoration actions. Advanced restoration actions are restoration actions that are:
carried out or intended to be carried out by a person before referring a proposal to take an action under section 68; and
directed at the protection, conservation or restoration of a matter protected by a provision of Part 3.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision for and in relation to the following matters:
registration of advanced restoration actions, including the publishing of any register;
applications for registration of advanced restoration actions, including fees for applications;
decisions by the Minister as to whether to register advanced restoration actions, including the nature of the actions that may be registered and any other requirements;
circumstances (not inconsistent with section 134) in which advanced restoration actions may satisfy conditions that may be attached to approvals under Part 9;
variation, suspension, revocation and transfer of registration of advanced restoration actions;
monitoring of registered advanced restoration actions;
record keeping and reporting in relation to registered advanced restoration actions.
Omit “person responsible for the adoption or implementation of”, substitute “responsible person for”.
Omit “bioregional plans”, substitute “bioregional guidance plans”.

section.heading: Minister may make bioregional guidance plans

content.p: (1) The Minister may make a written instrument under this subsection (a bioregional guidance plan).
(2) A bioregional guidance plan must specify the area (the region) to which it relates, which must be in one or more of the following:
a Commonwealth area;
a State;
a Territory.
A bioregional guidance plan may include provisions about one or more of the matters specified in section 176A.
The Minister may, by written instrument, vary a bioregional guidance plan.
The Minister may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, cooperate with one or more of the following in preparing to make or vary, or in implementing, a bioregional guidance plan:
a State or a self-governing Territory;
an agency of a State or of a self-governing Territory;
any other person.
The cooperation may include giving financial or other assistance.

section.heading: Contents of bioregional guidance plans

content.p: A bioregional guidance plan for a region may include provisions about one or more of the following:
the components of biodiversity, and their distribution and conservation status in the region;
important economic and social values relevant to the region;
heritage values of places;
threats to matters that are protected by a provision of Part 3;
areas in the region that may be suitable for protection, conservation or restoration measures;
areas in the region that may be suitable for ecologically sustainable development (whether generally or for specified classes of action);
areas in the region that may be unsuitable for ecologically sustainable development (whether generally or for specified classes of action);
guidance on suitable management actions for listed threatened species or listed ecological communities in the region;
objectives relating to biodiversity and other values;
priorities, strategies and actions to achieve the objectives;
mechanisms for community involvement in implementing the bioregional guidance plan;
measures for monitoring and reviewing the bioregional guidance plan;
any other matters the Minister considers relevant.

section.heading: Requirements for making or varying bioregional guidance plans

content.p: The Minister must not make or vary a bioregional guidance plan that relates to an area that is wholly or partly within a particular State or Territory unless the State or Territory has agreed to its making or variation.

The Minister must not make or vary a bioregional guidance plan unless the Minister is satisfied that the bioregional guidance plan, or the bioregional guidance plan as varied, is consistent with any national environmental standards prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this subsection.

For purposes of making or varying a bioregional guidance plan, the Minister must have regard to any comments received in response to a notice under paragraph 176C(1)(b) in relation to the draft bioregional guidance plan or the proposed variation.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a variation of a minor or machinery nature.
A bioregional guidance plan is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Public consultation

content.p: Before making or varying a bioregional guidance plan, the Minister must publish on the Department’s website:
a draft of the bioregional guidance plan or the proposed variation, as applicable; and
a notice inviting comments on the draft bioregional guidance plan or the proposed variation within the period specified in the notice, which must be a period of at least 30 business days.
The Minister must not make a bioregional guidance plan until after the end of the period specified in the notice.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a variation of a minor or machinery nature.

section.heading: Minister must publish bioregional guidance plans

content.p: The Minister must publish each bioregional guidance plan, and each bioregional guidance plan as varied, on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after the plan is made or varied, as the case requires.

section.heading: Incorporation of instruments

content.p: Despite section 46AA of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, a bioregional guidance plan may apply, adopt or incorporate (with or without modifications) an instrument or other writing:
as in force at a particular time; or
as is in force or existing from time to time.
After “bioregional”, insert “guidance”.
After “bioregional”, insert “guidance”.
Insert:

division.heading: General requirements about contents of bioregional plans

content.p: Subdivision A—Minister may make bioregional plans

section.heading: Minister may make bioregional plans

content.p: (1) The Minister may, by written instrument, make a plan (a bioregional plan) under this section in accordance with the requirements of this Part.
Note: Division 2 sets out the consultation requirements and decision making processes for making bioregional plans.
(2) A bioregional plan must specify the area (the region) to which it relates, which must be in one or more of the following:
a Commonwealth area;
a State;
a Territory.
A bioregional plan must:
include the objectives of the bioregional plan; and
specify development zones and related matters in accordance with Subdivision B of this Division; and
specify bioregional restoration measures and related matters in accordance with Subdivision C of this Division; and
specify conservation zones and related matters in accordance with Subdivision D of this Division.
A bioregional plan must specify the day on which it commences, which must not be earlier than the day on which it is published on the Department’s website under section 177AR.
A bioregional plan must include any other matters prescribed by the regulations.

A bioregional plan for a region may include information about the environment in the region including, but not limited to, information about the biodiversity, heritage or cultural heritage of the region.
A bioregional plan is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Incorporation of instruments

content.p: Despite section 46AA of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, information included in a bioregional plan as mentioned in subsection 177AA(6) may apply, adopt or incorporate (with or without modifications) an instrument or other writing:
as in force at a particular time; or
as is in force or existing from time to time.

section.heading: When a bioregional plan is in force

content.p: A bioregional plan is in force throughout the period:
beginning on the day on which it commences under subsection 177AA(4); and
ending on the day on which it is revoked under section 177BG.
Subdivision B—Bioregional plans must specify development zones and actions

section.heading: Development zones

content.p: A bioregional plan for a region must specify one or more areas in the region that are development zones.
The boundary of a development zone must be specified having regard to each of the following:
the world heritage values of any declared World Heritage property;
the national heritage values of any National Heritage place;
the ecological characteristics of any declared Ramsar wetland;
the location and habitat of any of the following:
any listed threatened species;
any listed threatened ecological communities;
any listed migratory species;
the environment in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park;
the environment in any part of a Commonwealth marine area.

section.heading: Priority actions and impacted protected matters for development zones

content.p: (1) A bioregional plan must specify, for each development zone specified in the bioregional plan, one or more classes of actions (a priority class of actions) that can be taken in the development zone. Each action in such a class is a priority action in the class.
Note: It is an offence not to comply with a condition attached to taking a priority action in a development zone, subject to specified exceptions: see section 177BZ.

(2) Before a priority class of actions is specified, the Minister must be satisfied that, taken as a whole, the actions in the class have, will have or are likely to have a significant impact on one or more matters protected by a provision of Part 3. Each such matter is an impacted protected matter for the priority actions in the class.
The bioregional plan must specify, for each priority class of actions specified under subsection (1), the impacted protected matters for the priority actions in the class.
Priority actions must not include any action of a kind mentioned in section 140A.
A bioregional plan must not specify a priority class of actions that includes one or more fossil fuel actions.

section.heading: Bioregional plan registration charge for priority actions

content.p: A bioregional plan may specify the persons taking priority actions in a development zone specified in the plan who are exempt from paying a bioregional plan registration charge in accordance with the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (Restoration Charge Imposition) Act 2025.

section.heading: Conditions about taking priority actions

content.p: A bioregional plan may attach conditions to the taking by a person of a priority action included in a priority class of actions in a development zone specified in the plan.
Note: Section 177BZ provides for offences and civil penalties for failure to comply with conditions.

Before a condition is attached to the taking by a person of a priority action, the Minister must be satisfied that the condition relates to an impacted protected matter for priority actions in the priority class of actions, in either or both of the following ways:
the condition is necessary or convenient to protect the impacted protected matter (whether or not the protection is protection from priority actions in the class);

the condition is necessary or convenient to mitigate or repair damage to the impacted protected matter (whether or not the damage has been, will be or may be caused by the priority actions in the class).
The bioregional plan must specify, for each condition, the impacted protected matters to which the condition relates.

A condition that relates to an impacted protected matter for a priority action does not apply to the taking of the priority action by a person for whom the priority action is a designated priority action for the impacted protected matter.

If an impacted protected matter to which a condition relates ceases to be a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, the condition ceases to have effect to the extent that the condition relates to the impacted protected matter.
Subdivision C—Bioregional plans must specify bioregional restoration measures

section.heading: Bioregional restoration measures

content.p: (1) A bioregional plan for a region must specify measures for the region (bioregional restoration measures) that the Minister is satisfied are necessary or convenient to mitigate, repair or compensate for likely damage to one or more impacted protected matters that has been, will be or may be caused by priority actions.

(2) A bioregional plan for a region may specify measures for the region (also bioregional restoration measures) that the Minister is satisfied are appropriate to protect or conserve one or more matters protected by a provision of Part 3 (whether or not the protection or conservation relates to priority actions).
(3) A bioregional restoration measure may include (without limitation) a measure providing for the payment of a specified amount (a bioregional plan restoration contribution).
For each bioregional restoration measure, the bioregional plan must specify one or more of the following persons to be responsible for ensuring delivery of the measure:
the Commonwealth;
a Commonwealth agency;
if a State has consented to be specified—the State;
if a Territory has consented to be specified—the Territory;
any other person who has consented to be specified.
To avoid doubt, a bioregional plan may specify that the Restoration Contributions Holder is responsible for delivering a bioregional restoration measure on behalf of the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Conditions about delivery of bioregional restoration measures

content.p: A bioregional plan for a region may include the following conditions relating to bioregional restoration measures:
conditions requiring the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure by a person specified in the bioregional plan to be responsible for the delivery;
conditions relating to the delivery of such a bioregional restoration measure by the person (including, but not limited to, how it is to be delivered).
Note: Division 7 provides for offences and civil penalties for failure to comply with conditions.

However, a condition must not require the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure by a person other than the Commonwealth or a Commonwealth agency unless the person has consented to the condition.

If an impacted protected matter to which a condition relates ceases to be a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, the condition ceases to have effect to the extent that the condition relates to the impacted protected matter.
Subdivision D—Bioregional plans must specify conservation zones

section.heading: Conservation zones

content.p: A bioregional plan for a region must specify one or more areas in the region that are conservation zones.
The boundary of a conservation zone must be specified having regard to:
the following:
a declared World Heritage property;
a National Heritage place;
a declared Ramsar wetland;
a Commonwealth marine area;
the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park; and
the location and habitat of any of the following:
any listed threatened species;
any listed threatened ecological communities;
any listed migratory species.

section.heading: Restricted actions and restricted protected matters

content.p: (1) A bioregional plan must specify, for each conservation zone in the bioregional plan, one or more classes of actions that are prohibited in the conservation zone. Each action in such a class is a restricted action in the class.

(2) Before a class of actions is specified, the Minister must be satisfied that, taken as a whole, the actions in the class have, will have, or are likely to have, a significant impact on one or more matters protected by a provision of Part 3. Each such matter is a restricted protected matter for the restricted actions in the class.
The bioregional plan must specify, for each class of actions, the restricted protected matters for the restricted actions in the class.

division.heading: Process for making a bioregional plan

section.heading: Minister must notify and seek comments on draft of a bioregional plan before it is made

content.p: Before the Minister makes a bioregional plan, the Minister must publish on the Department’s website:
a draft of the bioregional plan; and
a notice inviting comments on the draft bioregional plan within the period specified in the notice, which must be a period of at least 30 business days.
Before the Minister makes a bioregional plan, the Minister must seek the advice of the CEO.
Before the Minister makes a bioregional plan, the Minister may obtain advice from the following:
the Australian Heritage Council;
a committee established under Part 19.
The Minister must not make a bioregional plan until after the latest of the following:
the end of the period specified in the notice given under paragraph (1)(b);
the day on which the advice of the CEO is received.

section.heading: Matters to which the Minister must have regard in deciding whether to make a bioregional plan

content.p: For the purposes of deciding whether or not to make a bioregional plan, the Minister must have regard to the following:
the principles of ecologically sustainable development;
social and economic matters that the Minister considers relevant;
any bioregional guidance plans that the Minister considers relevant;
comments received in response to a notice on the draft bioregional plan that the Minister considers relevant;
any advice obtained from the CEO;
any advice obtained from the following:
the Australian Heritage Council;
a committee established under Part 19;
any approved conservation advice that the Minister considers relevant;
any recovery plan that the Minister considers relevant;
any matters prescribed by the regulations.
Note: These matters are also relevant to variations of bioregional plans (see section 177AX).

section.heading: Matters of which the Minister must be satisfied before making a bioregional plan—agreement of persons

content.p: The Minister must not make a bioregional plan for a region unless the Minister is satisfied:
that the bioregional plan has been agreed to by each relevant State and relevant Territory for the bioregional plan; and

if the bioregional plan includes one or more conditions relating to the delivery of bioregional restoration measures by a person other than the Commonwealth or a Commonwealth agency—that the person has consented to the imposition of the conditions.

section.heading: Matters of which the Minister must be satisfied before making a bioregional plan—protection statements and recovery plans

content.p: If the Minister considers that there is a protection statement that is relevant to a bioregional plan that the Minister proposes to make, the Minister must not make the bioregional plan unless the Minister is satisfied that the bioregional plan is not inconsistent with the protection statement.

If the Minister does not consider that there is a protection statement that is relevant to a bioregional plan that the Minister proposes to make, but considers that there is a recovery plan that is relevant to the bioregional plan, the Minister must not make the bioregional plan unless the Minister is satisfied that the bioregional plan is not inconsistent with the recovery plan.

If the Minister considers that there is a protection statement and a recovery plan that are relevant to a bioregional plan that the Minister proposes to make, the Minister must not make the bioregional plan unless the Minister is satisfied that the bioregional plan is not inconsistent with the protection statement, but is not required to be satisfied that the bioregional plan is not inconsistent with the recovery plan.

section.heading: Matters of which the Minister must be satisfied before making a bioregional plan—outcomes of the bioregional plan

content.p: The Minister must not make a bioregional plan for a region unless the Minister is satisfied of the following:
that making the bioregional plan will promote the objects of this Act;
that threats to matters protected by a provision of Part 3 in the region have been identified and addressed as appropriate, being threats arising other than from priority actions;
that the bioregional plan includes objectives directed at promoting the protection, conservation or restoration of the following (to the extent relevant to the bioregional plan):
listed threatened species;
listed threatened ecological communities;
listed migratory species;
the world heritage values of a declared World Heritage property;
the National Heritage values of a National Heritage place;
the ecological character of a declared Ramsar wetland;
the environment, in respect of the impact of a radiological exposure action;
the environment in a Commonwealth marine area;
the environment in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park;
a water resource, in respect of the impact of an action involving unconventional gas development or large coal mining development;
the environment on Commonwealth land;
that the bioregional plan will not have an unacceptable impact on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;

that the bioregional plan will, or will be likely to, result in the residual significant impacts of each priority class of actions (taken as a whole) on impacted protected matters being compensated to a net gain (within the meaning of paragraph 527K(1)(b) or (2)(b), as the case requires);
that the bioregional plan includes consideration of:
the expected impacts of climate change; and
appropriate adaptation and resilience measures to protect matters protected by a provision of Part 3 in response to those impacts.
Note: See the definition of unacceptable impacts in section 527F.

section.heading: Matters of which the Minister must be satisfied before making a bioregional plan—consistency with international conventions and other instruments

content.p: The Minister must not make a bioregional plan unless the Minister is satisfied that making the bioregional plan would not be inconsistent with any of the following:
Australia’s obligations under a designated international agreement;
any threat abatement plan the Minister considers relevant;
a designated environmental instrument.

The Minister must not make a bioregional plan unless the Minister is satisfied that making the bioregional plan would be consistent with any national environmental standards prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this subsection.

section.heading: Minister must publish bioregional plan

content.p: The Minister must publish each bioregional plan, and the reasons for the decision to make the bioregional plan, on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after the plan is made.
Subdivision A—Process for varying bioregional plans

section.heading: Minister may vary a bioregional plan in certain circumstances

content.p: The Minister may vary a bioregional plan for a region if the Minister is satisfied that one or more of the following applies:
a review of the bioregional plan has recommended the bioregional plan be varied;
the objectives of the bioregional plan are not being met;
both:
an ecological event has occurred that has had, will have, or is likely to have, a significant impact on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3; and
varying the bioregional plan is reasonably necessary to protect, or lessen any threats to, a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
there has been a change in development pressures in the region and varying the bioregional plan is appropriate in the circumstances;
both:
significant new information about a threat to a matter protected by a provision of Part 3 is available; and
having regard to the new information, varying the bioregional plan is reasonably necessary to protect, or lessen the threat to, a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
one or more priority actions taken have had or will have an unacceptable impact on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
Note: See the definition of unacceptable impacts in section 527F.

the bioregional plan has not resulted, or is not likely to result, in the residual significant impacts of each priority class of actions (taken as a whole) on one or more impacted protected matters being compensated to a net gain (within the meaning of paragraph 527K(1)(b) or (2)(b), as the case requires);
both:

there has been a change in a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, or in the status of a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, or in the importance of the population of a matter protected by a provision of Part 3; and
varying the bioregional plan is reasonably necessary to protect, or lessen any threats to, a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
both:
an action taken within or outside the region has had, or is likely to have, a significant impact on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3 in the region; and
varying the bioregional plan is reasonably necessary to protect, or lessen any threats to, a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
a condition of the bioregional plan relating to the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure has been, or is likely to be, contravened;
a bioregional restoration measure is no longer appropriate to achieve its purpose;
both:

an existing condition of the bioregional plan in relation to the taking of a priority action by a person is no longer necessary or convenient to protect, or to mitigate or repair damage to, an impacted protected matter to which the existing condition relates; and
the variation of the bioregional plan is to vary or revoke the existing condition;
the variation has been agreed to by:
each relevant State and relevant Territory for the bioregional plan; or
if the region is wholly located in one or more Commonwealth areas—the Commonwealth;
the variation is to a part of the bioregional plan that does not have regulatory effect;
the variation is necessary to ensure that the bioregional plan is consistent with a national environmental standard prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of subsection 177AQ(2);
a ground prescribed by the regulations exists.
The Minister may vary a bioregional plan for a region during a period when the bioregional plan is suspended under Division 4.

Without limiting paragraph (1)(j), a reference to a change in a matter protected by a provision of Part 3 includes the occurrence of a listing event (within the meaning of subsection 158A(1)) in relation to the matter.

section.heading: Scope of variations of a bioregional plan

content.p: Without limiting this Division, a variation of a bioregional plan may relate to one or more of the following:
development zones;
conservation zones;
priority actions;
impacted protected matters;
restricted actions;
restricted protected matters;
bioregional restoration measures;
conditions of the bioregional plan.
A variation of a bioregional plan may:
be minor or machinery in nature; or
relate to a provision of the bioregional plan that does not have regulatory effect.

section.heading: Requirements for variation to specify new impacted protected matters

content.p: The Minister must not vary a bioregional plan to specify a new impacted protected matter for an existing priority class of actions, without varying the existing priority class of actions, unless the Minister is satisfied that, taken as a whole, the actions in the class have, will have, or are likely to have, a significant impact on the new impacted protected matter.

Note: If the priority class of actions is also being varied in such a way that impacted protected matters are varied because of the application of section 177AE, the significant impact tests in those provisions will apply because of the operation of paragraph 177AX(1)(f).

section.heading: Requirements for variation to specify new restricted protected matters

content.p: The Minister must not vary a bioregional plan to specify a new restricted protected matter for an existing class of actions unless the Minister is satisfied that, taken as a whole, the actions in the class have, will have, or are likely to have, a significant impact on the new restricted protected matters.

Note: If the class of actions is also being varied in such a way that restricted protected matters are varied because of the application of section 177AE, the significant impact tests in those provisions will apply because of the operation of paragraph 177AX(1)(f).

section.heading: Consent requirements for variation of conditions of a bioregional plan

content.p: The Minister must not vary a bioregional plan in such a way that:
an existing condition requiring, or otherwise relating to, the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure by a person (other than the Commonwealth or a Commonwealth agency) is varied; or
a new condition requiring or otherwise relating to the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure by a person (other than the Commonwealth or a Commonwealth agency) is included;
unless the person has consented to the variation.

section.heading: Other matters relating to variations of a bioregional plan

content.p: In addition to the matters specified in this Division, for the purposes of deciding whether or not to vary a bioregional plan, the Minister must:
have regard to the matters specified in section 177AM (other than paragraphs 177AM(d) to (g)) in relation to the bioregional plan as proposed to be varied; and
have regard to any advice obtained from the CEO; and
have regard to any advice obtained from the following:
the Australian Heritage Council;
a committee established under Part 19; and
have regard to any comments received in response to a notice on the draft variation under section 177AY that the Minister considers relevant; and

ensure that the requirements in Division 1 and sections 177AN (agreement of persons), 177AP (outcomes) and 177AQ (consistency with instruments etc.) in relation to the bioregional plan as proposed to be varied are satisfied in relation to the bioregional plan as varied.
Note: The requirement for the Minister to ensure the matters in Division 1 are satisfied means, for example, that the Minister must ensure that:

any new or varied class of priority actions that can be taken in a development zone is specified in accordance with section 177AE, including that the bioregional plan specifies the impacted protected matters for the new or varied class; and

any new or varied development zone is specified in accordance with section 177AD and that the bioregional plan specifies classes of priority actions that can be taken in the zone and the impacted protected matters for each class in accordance with section 177AE; and

any new or varied condition in relation to the taking of a priority action by a person is attached in accordance with section 177AG, including that the bioregional plan specifies the condition and the impacted protected matters that the condition relates to.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a variation of a bioregional plan to the extent that the variation:
is minor or machinery in nature; or
relates to a provision of the bioregional plan that does not have regulatory effect.

section.heading: Minister must publish, notify and seek comments on a proposed variation of a bioregional plan

content.p: Before the Minister varies a bioregional plan for a region under section 177AS, the Minister must give a notice to the following:
each relevant State and relevant Territory for the bioregional plan;
each person who must comply with a condition of the bioregional plan in relation to the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure;
each registered person for the bioregional plan.
A notice under subsection (1) must:
state that the Minister proposes to vary the bioregional plan; and
include a draft of the proposed variation; and
specify the grounds on which the Minister proposes to vary the bioregional plan; and
invite comments on the draft variation within the period specified in the notice, which must be a period of at least 30 business days.
The Minister must:
publish a copy of a notice under subsection (1) on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after giving it; and
invite public comments on the draft variation within the period specified in the notice, which must be a period of at least 30 business days.
Before the Minister varies a bioregional plan, the Minister must seek the advice of the CEO.
The Minister must not vary a bioregional plan until after the latest of the following:
the end of the period specified in the notice given under paragraph (2)(d);
the end of the period specified in the notice given under paragraph (3)(b);
the day on which the advice of the CEO is received.
The Minister is not required to publish, notify or invite comments under this section on a draft of a proposed variation:
if the Minister reasonably believes that the variation is necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to human health or the environment; or
to the extent that the variation is minor or machinery in nature, or relates to a provision of the bioregional plan that does not have regulatory effect.
This section is taken to be an exhaustive statement of the requirements of the natural justice hearing rule in relation to a decision under section 177AS to vary a bioregional plan.

section.heading: Variation of a bioregional plan must be in writing, etc.

content.p: A variation of a bioregional plan must be in writing.

A variation of a bioregional plan must specify the day on which the variation commences, which must not be earlier than the day on which it is published on the Department’s website under section 177BA.
A variation of a bioregional plan is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Minister must publish, etc. bioregional plan as varied

content.p: The Minister must publish each varied bioregional plan for a region on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after varying the plan.
The Minister must also give a copy of the varied bioregional plan to the following:
each relevant State and relevant Territory for the bioregional plan;
each person who must comply with a condition of the bioregional plan in relation to the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure;
each registered person for the bioregional plan.
Subdivision B—Application of variations of bioregional plans to existing actions

section.heading: Variation of conditions—persons who have already registered priority actions

content.p: If the Minister varies a bioregional plan by attaching a new condition, or varying an existing condition, in relation to the taking of a priority action by a person, the new or varied condition does not apply to the taking of the priority action by the person if, immediately before the variation, the priority action was a registered priority action in relation to the person.

If a new or varied condition does not apply to the taking of a priority action by a person because of subsection (1), the Minister may, if the Minister considers it appropriate to do so, determine that the condition applies despite that subsection.
If the Minister makes a determination under subsection (2), the Minister must give the person written notice of the determination and the reasons for it.

The notice must specify the day the condition starts to apply to the taking of the priority action by the person (which must not be earlier than the day after the day the notice is given to the person).

section.heading: Variation of development zones—persons who have already commenced actions

content.p: This section applies to the taking of an action by a person if:
the Minister varies a bioregional plan by specifying a new development zone or varying an existing development zone; and
(b) the new or varied development zone covers an area (the new area) that was not a development zone immediately before the variation; and
before the variation:
the person commenced taking the action in the new area; or
the action was referred to the Minister under section 68, 69 or 71; and
immediately after the variation, the action is a priority action in relation to the new or varied development zone.

On and after the variation, a condition of the bioregional plan that would, but for this subsection, apply to the taking of the action by the person in the new area, is taken not to apply to the taking of the action by the person in the new area.
Note: The person is also not required to register the action (see subsection 177CB(4)).

section.heading: Variation of development zones—persons who have already registered priority actions

content.p: This section applies if:
the Minister varies a bioregional plan by removing or varying an existing development zone; and
(b) as a result of the variation, an area (the old area) that was covered by the existing development zone is no longer a development zone; and
immediately before the variation, a priority action in relation to the existing development zone was a registered priority action in relation to a person.

The bioregional plan as in force immediately before the variation (including any conditions of the plan) continues to apply to the person in relation to the taking of the action on and after the variation as if the variation had not happened.

section.heading: Variation of priority actions—persons who have already commenced actions

content.p: This section applies to the taking of an action by a person if:
the Minister varies a bioregional plan by specifying a new priority class of actions, or varying an existing priority class of actions, that can be taken in a development zone; and
before the variation:
the person commenced taking the action; or
the action was referred to the Minister under section 68, 69 or 71; and
immediately before the variation, the action was not a priority action; and
immediately after the variation, the action becomes a priority action because it is included in the new or varied class.

On and after the variation, a condition of the bioregional plan that would, but for this subsection, apply to the taking of the action by the person, is taken not to apply to the taking of the action by the person.
Note: The person is also not required to register the action (see subsection 177CB(4)).

section.heading: Variation of actions—persons who have already registered actions

content.p: This section applies if:
the Minister varies a bioregional plan by removing or varying an existing priority class of actions that can be taken in a development zone; and
as a result of the variation, an action that was included in the existing class is no longer included in any priority class of actions that can be taken in the development zone; and
before the variation, a priority action in relation to the development zone was a registered priority action in relation to a person.

The bioregional plan as in force immediately before the variation (including any conditions of the plan) continues to apply to the taking of the action by the person on and after the variation as if the variation had not happened.

division.heading: Suspension and revocation of bioregional plans

content.p: Subdivision A—Process for suspending or revoking bioregional plans

section.heading: Minister may suspend or revoke a bioregional plan

content.p: Power to suspend or revoke
The Minister may suspend or revoke a bioregional plan for a region if the Minister is satisfied that one or more of the following apply:
a review of the bioregional plan has recommended the bioregional plan be suspended or revoked;
the objectives of the bioregional plan are not being met;
there has been a change in development pressures in the region and suspending or revoking the bioregional plan is appropriate in the circumstances;
both:
an ecological event has occurred that has had, will have, or is likely to have, a significant impact on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3; and
suspending or revoking the bioregional plan is reasonably necessary to protect, or lessen any threats to, a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
both:
significant new information about a threat to a matter protected by a provision of Part 3 is available; and
having regard to the new information, suspending or revoking the bioregional plan is reasonably necessary to protect, or lessen the threat to, a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
one or more priority actions taken have had or will have an unacceptable impact on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
Note: See the definition of unacceptable impacts in section 527F.

the bioregional plan has not resulted, or is not likely to result, in the residual significant impacts of each priority class of actions (taken as a whole) on one or more impacted protected matters being compensated to a net gain (within the meaning of paragraph 527K(1)(b) or (2)(b), as the case requires);
both:

there has been a change in a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, in the status of a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, or in the importance of the population of a matter protected by a provision of Part 3; and
suspending or revoking the bioregional plan is reasonably necessary to protect, or lessen any threats to, a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
both:
an action taken within or outside the region has had, or is likely to have, a significant impact on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3 in the region; and
suspending or revoking the bioregional plan is reasonably necessary to protect, or lessen any threats to, a matter protected by a provision of Part 3;
a condition of the bioregional plan relating to the delivery of bioregional restoration measures has been, or is likely to be, contravened;
the suspension or revocation has been agreed to by:
each relevant State and relevant Territory for the bioregional plan; or
if the region is wholly located in one or more Commonwealth areas—the Commonwealth;
a ground prescribed by the regulations exists.
Effect of suspension of a bioregional plan—no new registrations

The effect of a suspension of a bioregional plan is that the Minister must not register a priority action under section 177BN, or transfer a registration under section 177BO, in a development zone specified in the bioregional plan during the period of suspension.
The suspension of a bioregional plan does not otherwise affect the operation of the bioregional plan, which remains in effect for all other purposes.
Meaning of change in a matter

Without limiting subparagraph (1)(h)(i), a reference to a change in a matter protected by a provision of Part 3 includes, but is not limited to, a reference to the occurrence of a listing event (within the meaning of subsection 158A(1)) in relation to the matter.

section.heading: Minister must notify and seek comments on proposed suspension or revocation of a bioregional plan

content.p: Before the Minister suspends or revokes a bioregional plan for a region under section 177BG, the Minister must give a notice to the following:
each relevant State and relevant Territory for the bioregional plan;
each person who must comply with a condition included in the bioregional plan in relation to the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure by the person;
each registered person for the bioregional plan.
A notice under subsection (1) must:
state that the Minister proposes to suspend or revoke the bioregional plan; and
specify the grounds on which the Minister proposes to suspend or revoke the bioregional plan; and
invite comments on the proposed suspension or revocation within the period specified in the notice, which must be a period of at least 30 business days.
The Minister must:
publish a copy of a notice under subsection (1) on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after giving it; and
invite public comments on the proposed suspension or revocation within the period specified in the notice, which must be a period of at least 30 business days.
The Minister must not suspend or revoke a bioregional plan under section 177BG until after the end of the period specified in paragraph (2)(c) or (3)(b) of this section, whichever is later.
Before suspending or revoking a bioregional plan, the Minister must seek the advice of the CEO.
Before suspending or revoking a bioregional plan, the Minister may obtain advice from the following:
the Australian Heritage Council;
a committee established under Part 19.

Despite subsections (1) to (4), the Minister is not required to publish, notify or invite comments on a draft of a proposed suspension or revocation of a bioregional plan if the Minister reasonably believes that the suspension or revocation is necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to human health or the environment.
This section is taken to be an exhaustive statement of the requirements of the natural justice hearing rule in relation to a decision under section 177BG to suspend or revoke a bioregional plan.

section.heading: Minister must publish and notify suspension of a bioregional plan

content.p: (1) If the Minister suspends a bioregional plan for a region under section 177BG, the Minister must give written notice of the suspension (a suspension notice) to the following as soon as practicable after the suspension:
each relevant State and relevant Territory for the bioregional plan;
each person who must comply with a condition of the bioregional plan in relation to the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure;
each registered person for the bioregional plan.
The suspension notice must specify:
the grounds for the suspension; and
the day the suspension takes effect (which must not be earlier than the day after the day the last notice is given under subsection (1)); and
either:
the things that must be done for the suspension to end (see subsection (3)); or
a fixed period for the suspension.
For the purposes of subparagraph (2)(c)(i), the things may be one or more specified things to be done by the Commonwealth, a relevant State or a relevant Territory for the bioregional plan.
The Minister must publish a copy of a notice under subsection (1) on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after giving it.

section.heading: Period of suspension

content.p: Suspension notices specifying fixed period
If a suspension notice specifies a fixed period for the suspension, the suspension ceases to have effect immediately after the end of the fixed period.
Suspension notices requiring things to be done
If a suspension notice specifies things that a person must do for the suspension to end:
the Minister must give the person a written notice as soon as practicable after the Minister is satisfied the person has done those things; and
the suspension ceases to have effect at the start of the day the Minister gives the person the notice under paragraph (a).
As soon as practicable after giving a notice under paragraph (2)(a), the Minister must:
