give each person mentioned in subsection 177BI(1) a copy of the notice; and
publish a copy of the notice on the Department’s website.

section.heading: Minister must publish and notify revocation of a bioregional plan

content.p: If the Minister revokes a bioregional plan under section 177BG, the Minister must give written notice of the revocation to the following as soon as practicable after the revocation:
each relevant State and relevant Territory for the bioregional plan;
each person who must comply with a condition of the bioregional plan in relation to the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure;
each registered person for the bioregional plan.
The notice must specify:
the grounds for the revocation; and
the day the revocation takes effect (which must not be earlier than the day after the day the last notice is given under subsection (1)).
The Minister must publish a copy of a notice under subsection (1) on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after giving it.
Subdivision B—Application of suspended or revoked bioregional plans to existing actions

section.heading: Application of bioregional plan to actions commenced during suspension period

content.p: This section applies to an action taken by a person if, during the period starting when a bioregional plan is suspended and ending when the suspension ceases:
the person commences taking the action in a development zone specified in the bioregional plan; or
the action is referred to the Minister under section 68, 69 or 71.

If, as a result of the suspension ceasing, the action would, but for this subsection, become a priority action in relation to a development zone specified in the bioregional plan, the action is taken not to be a priority action in relation to the development zone, to the extent that the action is taken by the person.

section.heading: Continuation of a revoked bioregional plan in relation to certain matters

content.p: This section applies if:
before the revocation of a bioregional plan:
a person commences an action that is a priority action in relation to a development zone; and
the action is still a priority action in relation to the development zone under the bioregional plan as in force immediately before its revocation; or
immediately before the revocation of a bioregional plan, a priority action in relation to a development zone is registered in relation to a person.
On and after the revocation:
the bioregional plan as in force immediately before the revocation; and
any conditions included in the bioregional plan under section 177AG; and
section 37;
continue to apply to the taking of the action by the person as if the revocation had not happened (despite section 177AC) but, to avoid doubt, cannot be varied after that revocation.

On and after the revocation, any conditions included in the bioregional plan under section 177AI continue to apply as if the revocation had not happened (despite section 177AC) but, to avoid doubt, cannot be varied after that revocation.

section.heading: Registering priority actions

content.p: A person proposing to take a priority action in a development zone specified in a bioregional plan may request that the Minister register the priority action in relation to the person.
Note: A person who takes a priority action that is not registered may commit an offence (see section 177CB).
A request under subsection (1) must:
be in writing; and
be in the approved form (if any); and
be accompanied by the greenhouse gas emissions information for the priority action; and
be accompanied by the following:
the information or documents (if any) that the approved form specifies are required;
the information or documents (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
Note: For greenhouse gas emissions information, see subsection 84A(2).
If a person makes a request under subsection (1) for the Minister to register a priority action, the Minister must, as soon as practicable after receiving the request:
decide to register the priority action in relation to the person; or
refuse to register the priority action in relation to the person.
Note 1: The Minister must not decide to register a priority action during a period when the bioregional plan is suspended (see subsection 177BG(2)).
Note 2: The Minister is not required to make a decision until further information requested has been provided (see subsection 177BR(2)).
The Minister must not decide to register a priority action in relation to a person unless the Minister is satisfied:
that the priority action would not be a designated priority action for the person for any impacted protected matter; and
that all of the impacted protected matters for the priority action have not ceased to be protected matters; and
that the person is capable of complying with the conditions of the bioregional plan that would apply to the taking of the priority action by the person; and
that any other matters prescribed by the regulations are satisfied.

In deciding whether or not to register a priority action specified in a development zone in a bioregional plan, the Minister may consider whether the person is a suitable person to take the priority action in the development zone, having regard to:
the person’s history in relation to environmental matters; and
if the person is a body corporate—the history of its executive officers in relation to environmental matters; and
(c) if the person is a body corporate that is a subsidiary of another body or company (the parent body)—the history in relation to environmental matters of the parent body and its executive officers.
As soon as practicable after making a decision under subsection (3), the Minister must give the person:
written notice of the decision; and
if the decision is to register the priority action—the day on which the registration will cease to have effect under subsection 177BQ(2); and
if the decision is to refuse to register the priority action—the reasons for the decision.
If the Minister decides to register the priority action, the priority action:
becomes registered in relation to the person on the day the Minister makes the decision; and
remains registered in relation to the person until any of the following events occurs:
the day on which a transfer of the registration takes effect under subsection 177BO(7);
the day on which a revocation of the registration takes effect under subsection 177BP(3);
the day on which the registration ceases to have effect under subsection 177BQ(2).
As soon as practicable after making the decision, the Minister must publish, on the Department’s website:
a copy of the decision; and
if the decision is to register the priority action—the greenhouse gas emissions information for the priority action.

section.heading: Transfer of registration

content.p: (1) A person (the transferor) in relation to whom a priority action is registered may request that the Minister transfer the registration of the priority action to another person (the transferee).
The request must:
be in writing; and
be in the approved form (if any); and
be accompanied by the following:
the information or documents (if any) that the approved form specifies are required;
the information or documents (if any) prescribed by the regulations;
(iii) a copy of the written agreement of the transferee to the transfer.
The Minister must, as soon as practicable after receiving the request:
consent to the transfer of the registration to the transferee; or
refuse to consent to the transfer of the registration.
The Minister must not consent to the transfer unless the Minister is satisfied of the matters specified in paragraphs 177BN(4) (a), (b), (c) and (d) in relation to the transferee.

In considering whether to consent to the transfer, the Minister may consider whether the transferee is a suitable person to take the priority action in the development zone specified in the bioregional plan, having regard to the matters specified in paragraphs 177BN(5)(a), (b) and (c) in relation to the transferee.
As soon as practicable after making a decision under subsection (3), the Minister must give the transferor and the transferee:
written notice of the decision; and
if the decision is to refuse to consent to the transfer—the reasons for the decision.

If the Minister decides to consent to the transfer, the notice under paragraph (6)(a) must specify the day on which the transfer takes effect, which must not be earlier than the day on which the notice is given.
If the Minister decides to consent to the transfer then, on and after the day specified by the Minister in accordance with subsection (7) as the day on which the transfer takes effect:
the priority action becomes registered in relation to the transferee; and
the priority action ceases to be registered in relation to the transferor; and

any conditions attached to the taking of the priority action that applied to the transferor immediately before that day cease to apply to the transferor on that day and apply to the transferee on and after that day.
If the Minister decides to consent to the transfer, the priority action remains registered in relation to the transferee until either of the following events occurs:
the day on which a transfer of the registration takes effect under subsection (7);
the day on which the registration ceases to have effect under subsection 177BQ(2).
The Minister must publish a copy of the decision on the Department’s website as soon as reasonably practicable after making the decision.

section.heading: Revocation of registration

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, revoke the registration of a priority action in relation to a person if the Minister is satisfied that:
the action is a priority action for an impacted protected matter; and
the person has failed to comply with a condition that relates to the impacted protected matter that is attached by the bioregional plan to the taking of the priority action; and
the condition applies to the taking of the priority action by the person.
The Minister must, as soon as practicable after revoking the registration:
give the person a notice that includes:
a copy of the instrument of revocation; and
the reasons for the revocation; and
publish the instrument of revocation, and the reasons for the revocation, on the Department’s website.
The revocation takes effect on the day specified in the instrument (which must not be earlier than the day the instrument is given to the person).
An instrument made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Cessation of registration of priority actions

content.p: This section applies if:
the Minister decides under paragraph 177BN(3)(a) to register a priority action in a development zone in a bioregional plan; and
as at the end of the period of 5 years beginning when the Minister made the decision, the priority action has not substantially commenced.
The registration ceases to have effect at the end of the period.

However, if the Minister decides under section 177BQA to extend the date on which the registration ceases to have effect, the reference in paragraph (1)(b) to the end of the period of 5 years beginning when the Minister made the decision is taken to be a reference to the date decided by the Minister under section 177BQA.

section.heading: Extending date of cessation of registration of priority action

content.p: (1) At least 6 months before the fifth anniversary of the date of a notice given under subsection 177BN(6) (the initial notice) of a decision under paragraph 177BN(3)(a) to register a priority action, the Minister must give the person to whom the initial notice was given written notice that, if the priority action has not substantially commenced before the fifth anniversary, the registration of the priority action will cease to have effect under subsection 177BQ(2) on that anniversary.
The person may request the Minister to extend the date on which the registration will cease to have effect under subsection 177BQ(2). The request must:
be in writing; and
be in the approved form (if any); and
be accompanied by the following:
the information or documents (if any) that the approved form specifies are required;
the information or documents (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
The request must be made at least 20 business days before the fifth anniversary.
The Minister must make a decision on the request within 20 business days.

The Minister may, if satisfied that it is appropriate to do so, extend the date on which the registration will cease to have effect under subsection 177BQ(2) to a later date specified by the Minister. The later date must not be later than the tenth anniversary of the date of the initial notice.

If the Minister extends the date to a date that is sooner than the tenth anniversary of the date of the initial notice, the Minister may, if the Minister is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so, further extend the date, so long as the later date is not later than the tenth anniversary of the date of the initial notice.
The Minister may further extend the date under subsection (6) on one or more occasions (so long as no further later date is later than the tenth anniversary of the date of the initial notice).
As soon as practicable after the Minister decides a request under subsection (2), or extends a date under subsection (6), the Minister must:
give the person written notice of the Minister’s decision; and
publish a copy of the decision on the Department’s website.

section.heading: Minister may request further information for making decision

content.p: The Minister may:

request a person to provide any additional information that the Minister considers is relevant to making a decision on a request made by the person under subsection 177BN(1) that the Minister register a priority action in a development zone; or
request a person who is a transferor or transferee, in relation to a request under subsection 177BO(1), to provide any additional information the Minister considers is relevant to making a decision.
There is no limit to the number of times the Minister may request information under subsection (1) from a person in relation to a request.
If the Minister has requested more information under subsection (1), the Minister is not required to make the decision concerned until the information is provided.

section.heading: Withdrawal of request

content.p: A person may withdraw the following requests made by the person by written notice given to the Minister:
a request under subsection 177BN(1) that the Minister register a priority action in a development zone;
a request under subsection 177BO(1) that the registration of a priority action be transferred.

section.heading: Minister may grant exemptions for restricted actions taken in a conservation zone in certain circumstances

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, grant an exemption from the operation of section 177CC in relation to the taking of a restricted action in a conservation zone by a person:
on the Minister’s initiative; or
on application under section 177BU.
Note: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 177BY(1).
Despite subsection (1), the Minister must not grant an exemption in relation to the taking of a restricted action in a conservation zone if the restricted action is a fossil fuel action.
Content of exemption
The exemption must specify:
the restricted action; and
the person to whom the exemption applies; and
the period for which the exemption is in force.
The Minister must be satisfied that the period specified for the purposes of paragraph (2)(c) is reasonably necessary having regard to the basis for the exemption.
When exemption comes into force
An exemption comes into force at the start of the period specified for the purposes of paragraph (2)(c) (which must not be earlier than the day the exemption is made).
Not a legislative instrument
An exemption made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.
An exemption under this section may be made even if the bioregional plan for the conservation zone is suspended.

section.heading: Application for exemption

content.p: A person may apply to the Minister for an exemption from the operation of section 177CC in relation to the taking of a restricted action in a conservation zone by the person.
Note: Section 177CC imposes penalties for taking a restricted action in a conservation zone.
An application under subsection (1) must:
be in the approved form (if any) for the application; and
be accompanied by the following:
the information or documents (if any) that the approved form specifies are required;
the information or documents (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
Note: The requirements under this subsection are in addition to any other requirements under this Act for an application.
The Minister must decide whether or not to grant the exemption after taking any steps required by section 177BW (consultation).

section.heading: Grounds for grant of exemption

content.p: Before granting an exemption under section 177BT in relation to the taking of a restricted action in a conservation zone by a person, the Minister must be satisfied:
that exceptional circumstances exist that justify granting the exemption; or
that:
the taking of the action would result or be likely to result in an outcome; and
that outcome is in Australia’s national interest.
That outcome is the intended outcome for the national interest proposal that, under section 75C, the action is taken to be.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.

If the Minister proposes to grant the exemption on the Minister’s initiative, the Minister must also be satisfied that the person proposing to take the action has agreed to the granting of the exemption.
Exceptional circumstances
In deciding for the purposes of paragraph (1)(a) whether or not exceptional circumstances exist that justify granting the exemption, the Minister must have regard to:
the extent to which the proposed restricted action would be consistent with the objectives of the relevant bioregional plan; and
the extent to which the proposed restricted action would achieve a conservation outcome; and
the extent to which the proposed restricted action is important for human safety; and
the extent to which the proposed restricted action would provide an essential economic, social or cultural outcome that cannot be achieved elsewhere; and
any comments made in response to a notice under paragraph 177BW(1)(a)(iii); and
any matters prescribed by the regulations; and
any other matters the Minister considers relevant.

section.heading: Consultation

content.p: Before deciding whether or not to grant an exemption from the operation of section 177CC in relation to the taking of a restricted action in a conservation zone, the Minister must:
publish the following (as applicable) on the Department’s website:
if an application has been made for the exemption—a copy of the application for the exemption (unless subsection (3) applies);
if the Minister proposes to grant the exemption on the Minister’s initiative—a copy of the draft of the exemption;
in any case (unless subsection (4) applies)—a notice inviting comments on the proposed exemption within the period specified in the notice, which must be a period of at least 30 business days; and
notify each State or Territory in which the whole or a part of the conservation zone is located.
Subject to subsection (4), the Minister must not decide whether or not to grant the exemption until after the end of the period specified in the notice published under subparagraph (1)(a)(iii).
The Minister must not publish under subparagraph (1)(a)(i) so much of the application as:
is:
(i) an exempt document under section 47 of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (trade secrets etc.); or

a conditionally exempt document under section 47G of that Act (business documents) to which access would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest for the purposes of subsection 11A(5) of that Act; or
the Minister believes it is in Australia’s national interest not to provide.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.
If the Minister is satisfied that granting the exemption is necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to human health or the environment:
the Minister is not required to publish a notice under subparagraph (1)(a)(iii); and
the Minister may make a decision to grant the exemption at any time.

section.heading: Notice of exemption decisions

content.p: This section applies if the Minister decides to grant an exemption from the operation of section 177CC in relation to the taking of a restricted action in a conservation zone by a person.
The Minister must, as soon as practicable after making a decision, give written notice of the decision and the reasons for the decision to the following (as applicable):
if the decision relates to an application under subsection 177BU(1)—the applicant;
if the decision is made on the Minister’s initiative—the person proposing to take the action;
in all cases—each State or Territory in which the whole or a part of the conservation zone is located.

The Minister must, as soon as practicable after giving written notice to the applicant or the person, as the case requires, publish a copy of the notice, and the reasons for the decision, on the Department’s website.
However, the Minister must not publish under subsection (3) so much of the reasons as:
is:
(i) an exempt document under section 47 of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (trade secrets etc.); or

a conditionally exempt document under section 47G of that Act (business documents) to which access would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest for the purposes of subsection 11A(5) of that Act; or
the Minister believes it is in Australia’s national interest not to provide.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.

section.heading: Minister may request information in relation to exemptions

content.p: The Minister may, by written notice, request any of the following persons (as applicable) to give the Minister information the Minister reasonably believes is relevant to making a decision on whether or not to grant an exemption from the operation of section 177CC in relation to the taking of a restricted action in a conservation zone:
if the decision relates to an application under subsection 177BU(1)—the applicant;
if the Minister is considering making the decision on the Minister’s initiative—the person proposing to take the action.
The notice given under subsection (1) must specify:
the information requested by the Minister; and
the day by which the information must be given to the Minister (which must be at least 10 business days after the day the notice is given to the person).
There is no limit to the number of times the Minister may request information under subsection (1) from a person.
If the Minister has requested more information under subsection (1), the Minister is not required to make the decision concerned until the information is provided.

section.heading: Non-compliance with general conditions of bioregional plans

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person does an act or omits to do an act; and
(b) doing the act, or omitting to do the act, contravenes a condition of a bioregional plan that is attached to the taking of a priority action (the relevant priority action); and
the relevant priority action is a registered priority action in relation to the person; and
the condition applies to, or in relation to, the taking of the relevant priority action by the person.
Exception—approval granted under Part 9 or such an approval is not required
Subsection (1) does not apply to an act or omission if:
an approval of the taking of the relevant priority action by the person is in operation under Part 9; or
a national interest exemption that allows the relevant priority action to be taken without an approval is in force; or
a provision of Part 4 allows the person to take the relevant priority action without an approval.
Exception—decision of Minister
Subsection (1) does not apply to an act or omission if:
there is in force a decision of the Minister under Division 2 of Part 7 that the relevant priority action is not a controlled action; and

if the decision of the Minister was made because the Minister believed that the relevant priority action would be taken in a manner specified in the notice of the decision given under section 77—the relevant priority action is taken in this manner.
Exception—relevant priority action commenced before bioregional plan came into effect
Subsection (1) does not apply to an act or omission if the person commences taking the relevant priority action before the bioregional plan came into effect.
Exception—relevant priority action referred to the Minister before bioregional plan came into effect
(5) Subsection (1) does not apply to an act or omission if:
at any time before the bioregional plan came into effect, the relevant priority action was referred to the Minister under section 68, 69 or 71; and
immediately before the bioregional plan came into effect:
the Minister had not yet decided under Division 2 of Part 7 whether the relevant priority action was a controlled action; or
the Minister had decided that the relevant priority action was a controlled action, but had not yet decided whether to approve the taking of the relevant priority action under section 133.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For the maximum pecuniary penalty for a contravention of a civil penalty provision of this Part, see section 481A.

section.heading: Non-compliance with conditions about bioregional restoration measures

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
a bioregional plan includes a condition requiring, or relating to, the delivery of a bioregional restoration measure by the person; and
the person contravenes the condition.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For the maximum pecuniary penalty for a contravention of a civil penalty provision of this Part, see section 481A.

section.heading: Requirement to register priority actions

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person takes an action; and
the action is a priority action for a development zone specified in a bioregional plan; and
the action is a priority action for an impacted protected matter; and
the action is not a registered priority action in relation to the person.
Exception—action in accordance with approval or approval not required
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if:
an approval of the taking of the action by the person is in operation under Part 9; or
a national interest exemption that allows the action to be taken without an approval is in force; or
a provision of Part 4 allows the person to take the action without an approval.
Exception—action in accordance with decision of Minister
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if:
there is in force a decision of the Minister under Division 2 of Part 7 that the action is not a controlled action; and
if the decision was made because the Minister believed that the action would be taken in a manner specified in the notice of the decision given under section 77—the action is taken in this manner.
Exception—action commenced before bioregional plan came into effect
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if the person commenced taking the action before the bioregional plan came into effect.
Exception for actions referred to the Minister before bioregional plan came into effect
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if:
at any time before the bioregional plan came into effect, the action was referred to the Minister under section 68, 69 or 71; and
immediately before the bioregional plan came into effect:
the Minister had not yet decided under Division 2 of Part 7 whether the action was a controlled action; or
the Minister had decided that the action was a controlled action, but had not yet decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133.
Other exceptions
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person that is a designated priority action for the person for all impacted protected matters.

Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if the impacted protected matter for which the action is a priority action has ceased to be a matter protected by a provision of Part 3.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For the maximum pecuniary penalty for a contravention of a civil penalty provision of this Part, see section 481A.

section.heading: Restricted actions must not be taken in conservation zones

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person takes an action; and
the action is a restricted action for a conservation zone specified in a bioregional plan; and
the action is a restricted action for an impacted protected matter.
Exception—action in accordance with approval or approval not required
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if:
an approval of the taking of the action by the person is in operation under Part 9; or
a national interest exemption that allows the action to be taken without an approval is in force; or
a provision of Part 4 allows the person to take the action without an approval.
Exception—action in accordance with decision of Minister
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if:
there is in force a decision of the Minister under Division 2 of Part 7 that the action is not a controlled action; and
if the decision was made because the Minister believed that the action would be taken in a manner specified in the notice of the decision given under section 77—the action is taken in this manner.
Exception—action covered by an exemption

Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if the person is covered by an exemption prescribed by the regulations made for the purposes of this subsection in accordance with subsection (12).
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if:

the action is a restricted action in relation to the conservation zone as a result of a variation of the bioregional plan that specified a new conservation zone or varied an existing conservation zone; and
(b) the new or varied conservation zone covers an area (the new area) that was not a conservation zone immediately before the variation; and
the person commenced taking the action in the new area before the variation.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if:

the action is a restricted action in relation to the conservation zone as a result of a variation to the bioregional plan that specified a new class of actions, or varied an existing class of actions, that are prohibited in the conservation zone; and
the person commenced taking the action before the variation.
Exception—action commenced before bioregional plan came into effect
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if the person commenced taking the action before the bioregional plan came into effect.
Exception for actions referred to the Minister before bioregional plan came into effect
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if:
at any time before the bioregional plan came into effect, the action was referred to the Minister under section 68, 69 or 71; and
immediately before the bioregional plan came into effect:
the Minister had not yet decided under Division 2 of Part 7 whether the action was a controlled action; or
the Minister had decided that the action was a controlled action, but had not yet decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133.
Other exceptions
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if the action is a designated restricted action for the person for all restricted protected matters.

Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if the restricted protected matter for which the action is a restricted action has ceased to be a matter protected by a provision of Part 3.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of an action by a person if an exemption under section 177BT in relation to the taking of the action by the person is in force.
Exemption prescribed by the regulations
Before making regulations prescribing an exemption for the purposes of subsection (4), the Minister must be satisfied that prescribing the exemption would not be inconsistent with:
the objects of this Act; and
the objectives of any bioregional plans that are in force; and
Australia’s obligations under a designated international agreement.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Note: For the maximum pecuniary penalty for a contravention of a civil penalty provision of this Part, see section 481A.

section.heading: Review of a bioregional plan

content.p: The Minister must cause reviews of each bioregional plan to be undertaken in accordance with this section.
The first review of a bioregional plan must commence within 5 years of the day on which the bioregional plan commences.
Subsequent reviews of a bioregional plan must commence within 5 years of the day on which a report of the previous review of the bioregional plan is given to the Minister under subsection (6).
A review of a bioregional plan must deal with the following matters:
the extent to which the bioregional plan has promoted the objects of this Act;
the extent to which the bioregional plan has resulted in a net gain for impacted protected matters in the region to which the bioregional plan relates;
the extent to which the bioregional plan has achieved its objectives;
any other matters prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph;
any other matters directed in writing by the Minister.
A review of a bioregional plan may make recommendations in relation to the matters with which it deals.
The person conducting a review of a bioregional plan must give a written report of the review to the Minister as soon as practicable after the review is completed.

The Minister must prepare and publish the Government’s response to a review of a bioregional plan on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after the report of the review is given to the Minister under subsection (6).
If the review made any recommendations, the response prepared under subsection (7) must give reasons for accepting or rejecting the recommendations.

division.heading: Priority actions that are components of larger actions

section.heading: Determination in relation to priority action that is a component of larger action

content.p: (1) A person who proposes to take an action (the larger action) that includes a component that is a priority action, other than a component that is a registered priority action, may apply to the Minister for a determination that the component (the component action) is taken not to be a priority action.
The application must:
be made in writing; and
be made in the approved form (if any); and
include the information or documents prescribed by the regulations (if any).
If the Minister is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so, the Minister may, in writing, determine that the component action is taken not to be a priority action.
If the Minister makes a determination, the determination takes effect on the day specified in the determination (which must not be earlier than the day it is made).
If the Minister makes a determination, the Minister must, as soon as practicable:
give the person a copy of the determination; and
publish a copy of the determination on the Department’s website.
While a determination is in force under subsection (3) in relation to a component action, the component action is taken not to be a priority action despite any other provision of this Part.
Note: This has the effect that the larger action, including the priority action, may be referred under Part 7 for approval under Part 9—see section 71A.
If the Minister decides not to make a determination, the Minister must, as soon as practicable, give the person written notice of the Minister’s decision and the reasons for it.
A determination made under subsection (3) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Exclusion determination

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, determine that, despite any other provision of this Part, a specified priority action, other than a registered priority action, that a person proposes to take is taken not to be a priority action if the Minister is satisfied that:
the taking of the action has not substantially commenced; and
the taking of the action would result or be likely to result in an outcome; and
that outcome is in Australia’s national interest.
That outcome is the intended outcome for the national interest proposal that, under section 75B, the action is taken to be.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.
Despite subsection (1), the Minister must not determine that a specified action is taken not to be a priority action if the action is a fossil fuel action.
The Minister may make the determination:
if the person proposing to take the action agrees in writing—on the Minister’s initiative; or
on application under section 177CG.
The Minister must, as soon as practicable after making the determination:
give a copy of the determination to:
the person proposing to take the action; and
the applicant (if different from the person mentioned in subparagraph (i)); and
publish a copy of the determination on the Department’s website.
The determination takes effect on the day specified in the determination (which must not be earlier than the day the determination is made).
While a determination is in force under subsection (1) in relation to an action, the action is taken not to be a priority action despite any other provision of this Part.
Note: This has the effect that the action may be referred under Part 7 for approval under Part 9—see section 71A.
A determination made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Application for exclusion determination

content.p: Any of the following persons may apply to the Minister for a determination under section 177CF:
the person proposing to take the action as mentioned in subsection 177CF(1);
if the person proposing to take the action agrees in writing:
another Minister; or
a Minister of a State or Territory.
The application must:
be made in writing; and
be made in the approved form (if any); and
include the information or documents prescribed by the regulations (if any).
The Minister must decide whether to make the determination, or refuse the application, within 20 business days of the day the application is made.
If the Minister decides to refuse the application, the Minister must give the applicant written notice of the Minister’s decision, and the reasons for it, as soon as practicable.

section.heading: Request for information

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, request any person to provide specified information that the Minister reasonably believes is necessary in order to make an informed decision about whether or not to make a determination under section 177CF.

If the Minister makes a request under subsection (1) in respect of a decision in which there is an applicant, a day is not to be counted as a business day for the purposes of subsection 177CG(3) if it is:
on or after the day the Minister requested the information; and
on or before the day the Minister receives the last of the information requested.

section.heading: Revocation of exclusion determination

content.p: Revocation on request
The Minister must, by written instrument, revoke a determination under section 177CF in relation to an action if:
the person proposing to take the action, or the designated proponent (if any), has made a written request for the revocation; and
the Minister has not decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133; and
the Minister has not made a decision under Division 2 of Part 7 that the action is not a controlled action.
Revocation on Minister’s initiative
The Minister must, on the Minister’s initiative, by written instrument, revoke a determination under section 177CF in relation to an action if:
the Minister is no longer satisfied that the taking of the action would result or be likely to result in the intended outcome mentioned in subsection 177CF(1); and
the Minister has not decided whether to approve the taking of the action under section 133; and
the Minister has not made a decision under Division 2 of Part 7 that the action is not a controlled action.
Timing
A revocation comes into force on the day specified in the revocation (which must not be earlier than the day the revocation is made).
Not legislative instrument
A revocation made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Notice of revocation of exclusion determination

content.p: As soon as practicable after revoking, under section 177CI, a determination under section 177CF in relation to an action, the Minister must:
give a copy of the revocation to:
the person proposing to take the action; and
the designated proponent (if any); and
publish a copy of the revocation on the Department’s website.

section.heading: Effect of revocation of exclusion determination if Minister has decided action is a controlled action

content.p: At the time a determination under section 177CF in relation to an action is revoked under section 177CI, any determination that, under section 75B, was taken to have been made in relation to the action is also taken to be revoked.

part.heading: The Restoration Contributions Holder, Restoration Contributions Special Account and related matters

section.heading: Establishment

content.p: There is to be a Restoration Contributions Holder.

section.heading: Appointment

content.p: (1) The Restoration Contributions Holder is to be engaged under the Public Service Act 1999.
The Restoration Contributions Holder is to be an SES employee in the Department.
Note: The expression SES employee is defined in section 2B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.

section.heading: Staff

content.p: The staff assisting the Restoration Contributions Holder are to be APS employees in the Department who are made available for the purpose by the Secretary.

section.heading: Delegation

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder may, in writing, delegate all or any of the Restoration Contributions Holder’s functions or powers under this Act to an SES employee or acting SES employee in the Department.
Note: The expression SES employee is defined in section 2B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
In performing a delegated function or exercising a delegated power, the delegate must comply with any written directions of the Restoration Contributions Holder.

section.heading: Functions of the Restoration Contributions Holder

content.p: The functions of the Restoration Contributions Holder are, on behalf of the Commonwealth:
to deliver restoration actions in accordance with Subdivisions A and B of Division 2; and
to deliver bioregional restoration actions in accordance with Subdivision C of Division 2; and
to engage in activities (including, but not limited to, delivering restoration actions) in accordance with Subdivision D of Division 2; and
to develop management plans in accordance with Division 3; and
to monitor and evaluate the progress and outcomes of restoration actions and bioregional restoration actions on which the Restoration Contributions Holder has spent amounts; and
to maintain a public register in accordance with Division 4; and
to prepare annual reports in accordance with Division 5; and

if requested to do so by the Minister—to provide advice to the Minister relating to restoration contribution charge, including in relation to proposed conditions of approvals that would require the payment of such charge; and
if requested to do so by the Minister—to provide advice to the Minister relating to bioregional restoration measures, and bioregional plan registration charge; and
to perform any other functions that are conferred on it by this Act or any other law of the Commonwealth; and
to perform any other functions prescribed by the regulations.
The functions of the Restoration Contributions Holder include doing any of the following on behalf of the Commonwealth:
exercising any powers of the Commonwealth to enter into contracts for such purposes;
maintaining up to date records.

section.heading: Powers of the Restoration Contributions Holder

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder has power to do all things necessary or convenient to be done for or in connection with the performance of the Restoration Contributions Holder’s functions.
The Restoration Contributions Holder may invest money that:
is mentioned in paragraph 177DK(a), (b), (c) or (d); and
is not immediately required for the performance of the functions of the Restoration Contributions Holder;
in an investment of any of the following kinds:
securities of, or securities guaranteed by, the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory;
(d) a deposit with a bank (within the meaning of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013), including a deposit evidenced by a certificate of deposit;
(e) any other form of investment prescribed by rules made for the purposes of subparagraph 58(8)(a)(iii) of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013.

section.heading: Limitation on directions to Restoration Contributions Holder

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder is not subject to the direction of the Minister or the Secretary in relation to the functions of the Restoration Contributions Holder mentioned in paragraphs 177CP(1)(a) to (c).

division.heading: Delivering restoration actions and bioregional restoration actions

content.p: Subdivision A—Restoration actions—general

section.heading: Spending on restoration actions

content.p: Application of this section

(1) This section applies if an amount of restoration contribution charge is imposed in relation to a particular residual significant impact (the primary impact) of an approved action, or an approved class of actions, on a matter (the affected matter) protected by a provision of Part 3 for which the approval has effect.
Default requirement for general restoration action

The Restoration Contributions Holder must spend an amount that reasonably relates to the amount of restoration contribution charge imposed to deliver a restoration action that the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied:
is directed towards protecting, conserving or restoring the affected matter in the bioregion where the affected matter is located; and
will result in a net gain (within the meaning of paragraph 527K(1)(b) or (2)(b), as the case requires) for the affected matter in that bioregion; and
complies with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations.

Note 1: For example, if an amount of restoration contribution charge is imposed in relation to the primary impact on a particular listed threatened species in a particular bioregion, an amount that reasonably relates to that amount must be spent on that listed threatened species in that bioregion (subject to subsection (4)).
Note 2: If an amount of restoration contribution charge has not yet been received, top-up amounts can be used: see section 177DB.

(3) A restoration action that satisfies paragraphs (2)(a), (b) and (c) is a general restoration action for the primary impact of the approved action or approved class of actions on the affected matter.
Alternative restoration action if default requirement is not met
Subject to section 177CT (which covers the situation in which subsection (2) is partly satisfied but not wholly satisfied), if:

the Restoration Contributions Holder has considered under subsection (2) whether the Restoration Contributions Holder must spend an amount to deliver a general restoration action for the primary impact of the approved action or approved class of actions on the affected matter; and
the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that:
a general restoration action is not feasible for the primary impact of the action or the class of actions, as the case requires; or
a general restoration action would not provide the best environmental outcome for the primary impact of the action or the class of actions, as the case requires; and

if the regulations prescribe requirements that must be met in order for the Restoration Contributions Holder to deliver an alternative restoration action in relation to the primary impact of an approved action or approved class of actions—Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that those requirements are met;

the Restoration Contributions Holder must spend an amount that reasonably relates to the amount of restoration contribution charge imposed to deliver a restoration action (an alternative restoration action) for the primary impact of the approved action or approved class of actions on the affected matter, being a restoration action that meets the requirements of subsection (5).

A restoration action meets the requirements of this subsection for the primary impact of the approved action or approved class of actions on the affected matter if the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that the restoration action:
will benefit a matter protected by the same provision of Part 3 as the affected matter; and

so far as is reasonably practicable, is directed towards protecting, conserving or restoring a matter protected by the same provision of Part 3 as the affected matter in the bioregion where the affected matter is located; and
provides a net gain (within the meaning of paragraph 527K(1)(b) or (2)(b), as the case requires) for the matter protected by the same provision of Part 3 as the affected matter; and
complies with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
Note: A restoration action under this subsection could be a restoration action that benefits a matter that is the same as the affected matter but in a different bioregion from the affected matter.
Minister must be notified if no general restoration action

The Restoration Contributions Holder must notify the Minister, in writing, if the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that subsection (4) applies to the approved action or approved class of actions.
Section subject to sections 177CT and 177CV
This section has effect subject to sections 177CT (combining general restoration actions and alternative restoration actions) and 177CV (pooling amounts).

section.heading: Combination of general restoration action and alternative restoration action

content.p: (1) This section applies if the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that subsection 177CS(2) is partly, but not wholly, satisfied in relation to a particular residual significant impact (the primary impact) of an approved action, or an approved class of actions, on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3.
The Restoration Contributions Holder must:

first—to the extent that the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied as mentioned in subsection 177CS(2), spend an amount that reasonably relates to the amount of restoration contribution charge imposed in relation to the primary impact on delivering a general restoration action for the primary impact; and

secondly—to the extent that the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied as mentioned in subsection 177CS(4), spend any remaining amount that reasonably relates to the amount of restoration contribution charge imposed in relation to the primary impact on delivering an alternative restoration action for the primary impact.
Note: If an amount of restoration contribution charge has not yet been received, top-up amounts can be used: see section 177DB.

section.heading: No requirement to spend restoration contribution charge if residual significant impact already compensated

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder is not required by section 177CS or 177CT to spend an amount that reasonably relates to the amount of restoration contribution charge imposed in relation to a residual significant impact (the primary impact) of an approved action, or an approved class of actions, on an affected matter if the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that the primary impact has already been compensated for by previous expenditure from money standing to the credit of the Restoration Contributions Special Account.

section.heading: Pooling amounts to cover multiple residual significant impacts

content.p: (1) The Restoration Contributions Holder may spend an amount (the aggregated amount) that is the sum of amounts that reasonably relate to amounts of restoration contribution charge imposed in relation to the residual significant impacts of one or more approved actions, or one or more approved classes of actions, on a matter or matters protected by a provision of Part 3, if:
the aggregated amount is spent to deliver one or more restoration actions to compensate for those impacts; and
the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that there will be a better environmental outcome for each of the matters if the aggregated amount were spent than would otherwise be achieved.
Note: If an amount of restoration contribution charge has not yet been received, top-up amounts can be used: see section 177DB.
The aggregated amount must be spent in accordance with sections 177CS and 177CT.

section.heading: Consultation with the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee on proposed restoration actions

content.p: Consultation not required if general restoration action feasible etc.

If the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that the Restoration Contributions Holder may deliver a general restoration action to compensate for a residual significant impact of one or more approved actions, or one or more approved classes of actions, on a matter or matters protected by a provision of Part 3, the Restoration Contributions Holder may, but is not required to, seek advice from the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee on appropriate restoration actions in relation to that impact.
Consultation required if general restoration action not available

If the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied as mentioned in subsection 177CS(4) in relation to a residual significant impact of one or more approved actions, or one or more approved classes of actions, on a matter or matters protected by a provision of Part 3, the Restoration Contributions Holder must seek advice from the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee on:
whether a general restoration action to compensate for the residual significant impact is feasible and would provide the best environmental outcome; and
if a general restoration action is not feasible or would not provide the best environmental outcome—an appropriate alternative restoration action for the residual significant impact.
The Restoration Contributions Holder may also consult the following in relation to restoration actions:
any other committee established under Part 19;
the Australian Heritage Council.

section.heading: Other matters to which the Restoration Contributions Holder must have regard

content.p: In spending an amount that reasonably relates to a restoration contribution charge on a restoration action (see paragraph 177CP(1)(a)), the Restoration Contributions Holder must have regard to the following:
any advice given by the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee in relation to the restoration action;
any advice given by:
any other committee established under Part 19; or
the Australian Heritage Council;
any approved conservation advice the Restoration Contributions Holder considers relevant;
any bioregional plan or bioregional guidance plan the Restoration Contributions Holder considers relevant;
any other matters the Restoration Contributions Holder considers relevant;
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
Subdivision B—Restoration actions—exemption amounts

section.heading: Spending exemption amounts on restoration actions

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder may spend amounts that reasonably relate to one or more amounts of exemption charge imposed on one or more restoration actions if:
the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that the restoration action or actions are:
for the purpose of protecting or conserving a matter or matters protected by a provision of Part 3; or
for the purpose of mitigating, repairing or compensating for damage to a matter or matters protected by a provision of Part 3; and
the spending of the amounts complies with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
Note 1: The Restoration Contributions Holder must also be satisfied of the matters specified in section 177DC.
Note 2: If an amount of exemption charge has not yet been received, top-up amounts can be used: see section 177DB.

For the purposes of subsection (1), it is not necessary that the matter or matters protected by a provision of Part 3 are likely to be impacted by an action for which the exemption concerned was granted.
The Restoration Contributions Holder:
may consult the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee in relation to appropriate restoration actions on which to spend amounts mentioned in subsection (1); and
if the Restoration Contributions Holder does so—must have regard to any advice given by the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee in spending such amounts.
Subdivision C—Bioregional restoration actions

section.heading: Spending on bioregional restoration actions

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder must, in performing functions relating to bioregional restoration actions that relate to spending amounts mentioned in subsection (2):
comply with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations; and
be satisfied of the matters (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
Note: The Restoration Contributions Holder must also be satisfied of the matters specified in section 177DC.
The amounts are as follows:
amounts that reasonably relate to amounts of bioregional plan registration charge imposed on the registration of one or more priority actions;
amounts that reasonably relate to amounts of bioregional plan restoration contribution required to be paid by a condition of a bioregional plan.
Note: If an amount of charge has not yet been received, top-up amounts can be used: see section 177DB.
The Restoration Contributions Holder:
may consult the following in relation to appropriate bioregional restoration actions:
the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee;
any other committee established under Part 19;
the Australian Heritage Council; and

if the Restoration Contributions Holder does so—must have regard to any advice given by the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee, the other committee or the Australian Heritage Council in making the decision.
Subdivision D—Top-up amounts

section.heading: Spending top-up amounts for activities

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder may spend top-up amounts on one or more activities (including but not limited to restoration actions) if:
the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that the activities are:
for the purpose of protecting or conserving a matter or matters protected by a provision of Part 3; or
for the purpose of mitigating, repairing or compensating for damage to a matter or matters protected by a provision of Part 3; and
the spending of the amounts complies with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
Note: The Restoration Contributions Holder must also be satisfied of the matters specified in section 177DC.
The Restoration Contributions Holder:
may consult the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee in relation to appropriate activities on which to spend amounts mentioned in subsection (1); and
if the Restoration Contributions Holder does so—must have regard to any advice given by the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee in spending such amounts.

section.heading: Spending top-up amounts for other purposes

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder may spend top-up amounts for the purposes of delivering restoration actions or bioregional restoration actions under Subdivision A, B, or C if:
the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that:
the spending of the top-up amounts is for the purpose of delivering restoration actions or bioregional restoration actions before amounts of charge have been received; or
it is otherwise appropriate to spend the top-up amounts; and
the spending of the top-up amounts complies with the requirements of Subdivision A, B or C before amounts of charge have been received.
Note: The Restoration Contributions Holder must also be satisfied of the matters specified in section 177DC.
Subdivision E—General

section.heading: Other matters of which the Restoration Contributions Holder must be satisfied

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder must not spend an amount on a restoration action, a bioregional restoration action, or any other activity unless the Restoration Contributions Holder is satisfied that spending the amount:
would promote the objects of the Act; and
would be consistent with any national environmental standard that is prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph; and
would not be inconsistent with Australia’s obligations under a designated international agreement; and
satisfies any other matters prescribed by the regulations.

section.heading: Management plans for restoration actions—restoration contribution charge

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder must develop a management plan for each restoration action on which one or more amounts that reasonably relate to amounts of restoration contribution charge imposed have been spent by the Restoration Contributions Holder under Subdivision A of Division 2.
The Restoration Contributions Holder must complete the management plan within the time period specified in the regulations (if any).
A management plan for a restoration action must specify the following:
each residual significant impact of an action or class of actions for which the restoration action is intended to compensate;
the action or class of actions for each such residual significant impact;
the holder of the approval for each such action or class of actions;
each matter protected by a provision of Part 3 that is likely to be damaged by each such residual significant impact;
whether restoration contribution charge imposed in relation to each such residual significant impact has been paid;
the restoration action that will be delivered;
the amounts that have been, or are being, spent on the restoration action;
the intended outcome or outcomes resulting from the restoration action;
the period within which the restoration action is to be delivered;
identification of risks and mitigation strategies in relation to the restoration action;

a schedule specifying monitoring, evaluation, reporting and adaptive management mechanisms, in order to ensure that the net gain for each matter protected by a provision of Part 3 that is likely to be damaged by each residual significant impact mentioned in paragraph (a):
is likely to be achieved within the required period; and
will be maintained;
which must be developed having regard to likely risks including, but not limited to, the likely effects of climate change;
evidence to support the restoration action as the preferred option.
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
The Restoration Contributions Holder must monitor progress and evaluate the outcomes of restoration actions delivered, having regard to the management plan for the restoration action.

section.heading: Management plans for bioregional restoration actions—bioregional plan registration charge and bioregional plan restoration contribution

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder must develop a management plan for each bioregional restoration action on which one or more of the following amounts have been spent by the Restoration Contributions Holder:
amounts that reasonably relate to amounts of bioregional plan registration charge imposed on the registration of priority actions;
amounts that reasonably relate to amounts of bioregional plan restoration contribution required to be paid by a condition of a bioregional plan;
top-up amounts.
The Restoration Contributions Holder must complete the management plan within the time period specified in the regulations (if any).
A management plan for a bioregional restoration action under this section must include the matters (if any) prescribed by the regulations.

The Restoration Contributions Holder must monitor progress and evaluate the outcomes of bioregional restoration actions delivered, having regard to the management plan for the bioregional restoration action.

section.heading: Management plans for restoration actions—exemption charge

content.p: The regulations may require the Restoration Contributions Holder to develop a management plan for each restoration action on which one or more amounts that reasonably relate to amounts of exemption charge imposed have been spent by the Restoration Contributions Holder.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision for and in relation to the following:
the matters to be included in a management plan;
the time period within which the Restoration Contributions Holder must complete a management plan;
other relevant matters.

If regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) require the Restoration Contributions Holder to develop a management plan, the Restoration Contributions Holder must monitor progress and evaluate the outcomes of restoration actions delivered, having regard to the management plan.

section.heading: Management plans for activities covered by section 177DA—certain top-up amounts

content.p: The regulations may require the Restoration Contributions Holder to develop a management plan for each activity on which one or more top-up amounts have been spent by the Restoration Contributions Holder.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision for and in relation to the following:
the matters to be included in a management plan;
the time period within which the Restoration Contributions Holder must complete a management plan;
other relevant matters.

If regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) require the Restoration Contributions Holder to develop a management plan, the Restoration Contributions Holder must monitor progress and evaluate the outcomes of restoration actions delivered, having regard to the management plan.

section.heading: Register to be established

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder must establish and maintain a register of the following:
all approved actions, and approved classes of actions, in relation to which amounts of restoration contribution charge have been imposed;
all bioregional plans in relation to which amounts of bioregional plan registration charge have been imposed on the registration of a priority action;
all bioregional plans that include a condition that requires a person to pay a bioregional plan restoration contribution;
all actions in relation to which amounts of exemption charge have been imposed.
Restoration contribution charge

The register must contain the following details in relation to each approved action, and each approved class of actions, in relation to which an amount of restoration contribution charge has been imposed:
details of each residual significant impact of the approved action, or approved class of actions, in relation to which an amount of restoration contribution charge has been imposed;
for each such residual significant impact:
each matter protected by a provision of Part 3 that is likely to be damaged by the residual significant impact; and
the amount of restoration contribution charge imposed in relation to the residual significant impact; and
whether the restoration contribution charge has been paid;
each restoration action on which an amount was spent to compensate for each such residual significant impact, and the amount spent on each such restoration action;
the intended outcomes of each such restoration action;
the management plan for each such restoration action;
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
Bioregional plan registration charge

The register must contain the details prescribed by the regulations in relation to each bioregional plan in relation to which an amount of bioregional plan registration charge has been imposed on a registered priority action.
Bioregional plan restoration contributions

The register must contain the details prescribed by the regulations in relation to each bioregional plan that includes a condition that requires a person to pay a bioregional plan restoration contribution.
Exemption charge
The register must contain the details prescribed by the regulations in relation to each action in relation to which an amount of exemption charge has been imposed.
Top-up amounts
The register must contain the details prescribed by the regulations in relation to each activity on which a top-up amount has been spent by the Restoration Contributions Holder under section 177DA.
The register must be made publicly available on the Department’s website.
The register is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Annual report

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Holder must cause to be prepared, as soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, an annual report on the exercise of the Restoration Contributions Holder’s functions and powers during the financial year.
Without limiting subsection (1), the annual report must include the following in relation to the financial year:
details of each residual significant impact of an approved action, or approved class of actions, in relation to which an amount of restoration contribution charge has been imposed;
details of each approved action, or approved class of actions, mentioned in paragraph (a);
for each such residual significant impact:
each matter protected by a provision of Part 3 that is likely to be damaged by the residual significant impact; and
the amount of restoration contribution charge imposed in relation to the residual significant impact; and
whether the restoration contribution charge has been paid;
details of each restoration action on which an amount was spent under Subdivision A or B of Division 2;
details of each bioregional restoration action on which an amount was spent;
details of each activity on which the Restoration Contributions Holder spent top-up amounts under section 177DA;
achievements against the objectives of the management plan for each restoration action and each bioregional restoration action, including progress towards a net gain (where relevant);
for any residual significant impacts of an approved action, or an approved class of action, for which a general restoration action was not available:
the residual significant impacts; and
the matters protected by a provision of Part 3 that are likely to be damaged by each such residual significant impact;
a reconciliation of monies from the Restoration Contributions Special Account against the relevant projects;
any directions given by the Minister or the Secretary to the Restoration Contributions Holder;
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
Note: Section 177CR limits the directions that may be given by the Minister or Secretary.
The Restoration Contributions Holder must give the annual report to the Minister as soon as practicable after it is prepared.
The Minister must publish a copy of the annual report on the Department’s website within 20 days of receiving the report.

section.heading: Restoration Contributions Special Account

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Special Account is established by this section.
(2) The Restoration Contributions Special Account is a special account for the purposes of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013.

section.heading: Credits of amounts to the Restoration Contributions Special Account

content.p: There must be credited to the Restoration Contributions Special Account amounts equal to the following amounts received by or on behalf of the Commonwealth:
amounts of restoration contribution charge;
amounts of bioregional plan registration charge;
amounts of exemption charge;
amounts of bioregional plan restoration contribution;
amounts received in connection with the performance of the Restoration Contributions Holder’s functions;

amounts of any gifts or bequests received by the Restoration Contributions Holder, or made for the purposes of the Special Account, not being gifts or bequests that are expressed to be tied to the granting of approval of a specific action, or are subject to any directions for expenditure;
amounts of interest earned on the investment, in accordance with subsection 177CQ(2), of amounts mentioned in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d) standing to the credit of the Special Account.

Note: An Appropriation Act may contain a provision to the effect that, if any of the purposes of a special account is a purpose that is covered by an item in the Appropriation Act (whether or not the item expressly refers to the special account), then amounts may be debited against the appropriation for that item and credited to that special account.

section.heading: Purposes of the Restoration Contributions Special Account

content.p: The purposes of the Restoration Contributions Special Account are as follows:
paying or discharging the costs, expenses and other obligations associated with the performance of the functions of the Restoration Contributions Holder;
paying or discharging the costs, expenses and other obligations associated with the performance of the functions of the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee;
paying any remuneration or allowances payable to the following:
the Restoration Contributions Holder;
APS employees assisting the Restoration Contributions Holder;
paying or discharging the costs, expenses and other obligations associated with an investment of a kind mentioned in subsection 177CQ(2).
Note: See section 80 of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 (which deals with special accounts).

hcontainer.heading: Section 267 (paragraph beginning “The Minister need ensure that a recovery plan”)

content.p: Omit the paragraph, substitute:

The Minister need ensure that a recovery plan is in force for the whole or part of a listed threatened species or ecological community only if the Minister decides to have a recovery plan for the whole or part of the species or community. The Minister must decide whether to have a recovery plan for the species or community, or part of it, within 90 days after it becomes listed. The Minister may, at any other time, decide whether to have such a plan.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Section 267 (paragraph beginning “The Minister need ensure a threat abatement plan”)

content.p: Repeal the paragraph, substitute:

The Minister need ensure a threat abatement plan is in force for the whole, or one or more parts, of a key threatening process only if the Minister decides that a plan is a feasible, effective and efficient way of abating the whole process or the relevant part or parts of the process. The Minister must consult before making such a decision.
Repeal the subsection, substitute:

Within 90 days after a listed threatened species (except one that is extinct or that is a conservation dependent species) or a listed threatened ecological community becomes listed, the Minister must decide whether to:
have a recovery plan for the whole species or ecological community; or
have a recovery plan for part of the species or ecological community; or
not have a recovery plan at all for the species or ecological community.

If the Minister decides to have a recovery plan for one or more parts of the species or ecological community, the Minister is taken to have also decided not to have a recovery plan for any other part of the species or ecological community.

The Minister may, at any other time, decide whether to have a recovery plan for a listed threatened species (except one that is extinct or that is a conservation dependent species) or a listed threatened ecological community, or part of such a species or ecological community.
