hcontainer.heading: After Subdivision B of Division 5 of Part 13

content.p: Insert:
Subdivision BA—Protection statements

section.heading: Protection statements for listed threatened species and listed threatened ecological communities

content.p: (1) The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make a protection statement for:
a listed threatened species or one or more parts of a listed threatened species (except one that is extinct or is a conservation dependent species); or
a listed threatened ecological community or one or more parts of a listed threatened ecological community.
The Minister must not make a protection statement unless the Minister is satisfied that the protection statement:
is consistent with any national environmental standard prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph; and
meets any criteria prescribed by the regulations.
In making a protection statement for a species or community or one or more parts of a species or community, the Minister must have regard to:
any recovery plan for the species or community or a relevant part of the species or community; and
any approved conservation advice for the species or community; and
any advice received from a person or body in accordance with section 298D; and
(d) any relevant comments received in accordance with section 298E; and
any matter prescribed by the regulations; and
any other matter the Minister considers relevant.

section.heading: Content of protection statements

content.p: A protection statement for a species or community or one or more parts of a species or community must include information about what must be protected in order to ensure the survival and recovery of the species or community, or the relevant parts of the species or community, in the wild.
A protection statement for a species or community or one or more parts of a species or community may also include:

information about impacts on the species or community, or a relevant part of the species or community, that would or would be likely to seriously impair the viability of the species or community or part of the species or community; or
information about critical habitat for the species or community, or a relevant part of the species or community; or
information about irreplaceable habitat for the species or community, or a relevant part of the species or community; or

information about whether payment of a restoration contribution charge should be available in relation to a residual significant impact that an action has, will have or is likely to have on the species or community or a relevant part of the species or community; or
any information the Minister considers relevant; or
any other information prescribed by the regulations.

A protection statement for a species or community or one or more parts of a species or community may also set out circumstances or factors that the Minister considers are relevant to the exercise of discretion (if applicable) by a decision maker in applying an environment law provision relevant to an impact on the species or community or part of the species or community.
298C Protection statements may cover more than one species or community
A single protection statement may cover:
one or more species or communities; or
one or more parts of the same, or different, species or communities; or
any combination thereof.

section.heading: Advice on protection statements

content.p: The Minister may obtain advice, in accordance with the regulations (if any), from any of the following persons or bodies before making, varying or revoking a protection statement:
the Scientific Committee;
the Restoration Contributions Holder;
the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee;
a State or Territory government body;
any other person or body the Minister considers relevant.

section.heading: Public consultation on protection statements

content.p: Before making or varying a protection statement, the Minister must publish on the Department’s website:
a draft of the protection statement or variation; and
a notice inviting comments on the draft protection statement or variation within the period specified in the notice, which must be a period of at least 30 business days.
The Minister must not make or vary a protection statement until after the end of the period specified in the notice.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a variation of a minor or machinery nature.

section.heading: Varying a protection statement

content.p: The Minister may, by legislative instrument, vary a protection statement if the Minister is satisfied it is appropriate to do so.
In varying a protection statement for a species or community or one or more parts of a species or community the Minister must have regard to:
(a) any recovery plan for the species or community or a relevant part of the species or community;
any approved conservation advice for the species or community; and
any advice received from a person or body in accordance with section 298D; and
(d) any relevant comments received in accordance with section 298E.
If the Minister varies a protection statement, the Minister must publish reasons for the variation on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after making the variation.

section.heading: Revoking protection statements

content.p: Automatic revocation
A protection statement for a species or community or one or more parts of a species or community is, by force of this section, revoked if:
the species or community ceases to be a listed threatened species or listed threatened ecological community; or
the species is transferred to the extinct category or the conservation dependent category.
The revocation takes effect at the time that the event mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) occurs.
Revocation by Minister
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, revoke a protection statement if the Minister is satisfied that the protection statement is no longer appropriate.
The Minister must have regard to any advice obtained from a person or body in accordance with section 298D in revoking a protection statement.
If the Minister revokes a protection statement, the Minister must publish reasons for the revocation on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after making the revocation.

section.heading: Reviews of protection statements

content.p: The Minister must cause reviews of each protection statement to be undertaken in accordance with this section.
The first review of a protection statement must commence within 5 years of the day on which the protection statement commences.
Subsequent reviews of a protection statement for a species or community or one or more parts of a species or community must commence:
if the Minister makes or varies a recovery plan for the species or community or a relevant part of the species or community—when the recovery plan is made or varied; and

if the Minister approves a conservation advice or changes an approved conservation advice for the species or community or a relevant part of the species or community—when the conservation advice is approved or changed; and
in all cases—within 5 years after the day on which a report of the previous review of the protection statement is given to the Minister under subsection (5).
A review of a protection statement must consider:
the matters prescribed by the regulations; and
any other matter specified by the Minister in writing.
The person conducting a review of a protection statement must give a written report of the review to the Minister within:
12 months after the day the review is commenced; or
a longer period determined in writing by the Minister.
The Minister must publish the report on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after the report is given to the Minister.
An instrument mentioned in paragraph (4)(b) is not a legislative instrument.
Insert:

division.heading: Exemptions from provisions of this Part

section.heading: Exemption from provisions of this Part

content.p: (1) The Minister may, by written instrument, grant an exemption (a Part 13 exemption) for an action from a provision (including a regulation made under a provision) of this Part:
on the Minister’s initiative; or
on application under section 302C.
Note: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 302N(1).
Content of exemption
The exemption must specify:
the action; and
each provision from which the action is exempt; and
the person to whom the exemption applies; and
the period for which the exemption is in force; and
any conditions imposed on the exemption under section 302E.
The Minister must be satisfied that the period specified for the purposes of paragraph (2)(d) is reasonably necessary to address the national interest that is the basis for the exemption.
When exemption comes into force
An exemption comes into force at the start of the period specified for the purposes of paragraph (2)(d) (which must not be earlier than the day the exemption is made).
Not a legislative instrument
An exemption made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Effect of Part 13 exemption

content.p: While a Part 13 exemption from a provision is in force for an action, the provision does not apply in relation to the taking of the action if:
the action is taken by the person to whom the exemption applies; and
the person takes the action in accordance with the conditions (if any) of the exemption.
Note 1: For conditions of an exemption, see section 302E.

Note 2: To the extent a defendant seeks to rely on this section as a defence to an offence, the defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this section: see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Application for Part 13 exemption

content.p: (1) The following may apply to the Minister (the Environment Minister) for a Part 13 exemption for an action:
the person who proposes to take the action;
if that person agrees in writing—a Minister (other than the Environment Minister), or a Minister of a State or Territory.
The application must:
be in writing; and
specify the provision or provisions from which the person is applying for an exemption for the action.
Timeframe for decision
The Minister must decide whether to grant the exemption under section 302A within 20 business days of receiving the application.

Note: If the Minister requests information to make an informed decision under section 302N, days between the request and receipt of the information do not count towards this timeframe (subsection 302N(2)).
Notice if Minister decides not to grant exemption
If the Minister decides not to grant the exemption, the Minister must give the applicant written notice of the Minister’s decision as soon as practicable after the decision is made.
Note: If the Minister grants the exemption, the Minister must give each person to whom the exemption applies a copy of the exemption (see section 302F).

section.heading: Grounds for grant of Part 13 exemption

content.p: Before granting a Part 13 exemption for an action from a provision (including a regulation made under a provision) of this Part the Minister must be satisfied that:
if the exemption were not granted, the action would contravene the provision; and
it is in the national interest that the provision not apply to the taking of the action by the person to whom the exemption is to apply.
In determining the national interest for the purposes of a provision of this Division, the Minister may consider:
Australia’s defence or security; or
(b) a national emergency, including an emergency to which a national emergency declaration (within the meaning of the National Emergency Declaration Act 2020) relates.
This does not limit the matters the Minister may consider.
Note: The following provisions of this Division require the Minister to consider the national interest:
paragraph (1)(b) of this section;
subsection 302G(3);
paragraph 302K(1)(a).

section.heading: Conditions of Part 13 exemption

content.p: The Minister may impose one or more conditions on a Part 13 exemption for an action from a provision if any of the following subsections apply.
Conditions—general
The Minister is satisfied that:
the provision is not a regulation made for the purposes of paragraph 301A(b), (c) or (d); and
the condition is necessary or convenient for protecting from the action, or mitigating damage that has been, will be or may be caused by the action to:

a listed threatened species, a listed threatened ecological community, a listed migratory species or a listed marine species, or the habitat of such a species or of such an ecological community, that is in a Commonwealth area; or
the environment in a Commonwealth area.
Conditions—cetaceans
The Minister is satisfied that:
the provision is not a regulation made for the purposes of paragraph 301A(b), (c) or (d); and
the action is likely to interfere with, or otherwise affect, cetaceans in, or in waters beyond the outer limits of, the Australian Whale Sanctuary; and
the condition is necessary or convenient for:
avoiding or mitigating the interference with or effect on the cetaceans that has been, will be or is likely to be caused by the action; or

protecting from the action, or mitigating damage that has been, will be or may be caused by the action to, the environment of, or the environment of waters beyond the outer limits of, the Australian Whale Sanctuary.
Conditions—bringing invasive species into Australia
The Minister is satisfied that:
the provision is a regulation made for the purposes of paragraph 301A(b); and
the condition relates to bringing a member of a species included in the list mentioned in paragraph 301A(a) into the Australian jurisdiction.
Conditions—trade in invasive species
The Minister is satisfied that:
the provision is a regulation made for the purposes of paragraph 301A(c); and
the condition relates to trade in members of a species included in the list mentioned in paragraph 301A(a):
between Australia and another country; or
between 2 States; or
between 2 Territories; or
between a State and a Territory; or
by a constitutional corporation.
Conditions—actions involving or affecting invasive species
The Minister is satisfied that:
the provision is a regulation made for the purposes of paragraph 301A(d); and
the condition:
involves or affects members of a species included in the list mentioned in paragraph 301A(a); and
is appropriate and adapted to give effect to Australia’s obligations under an agreement with one or more other countries.

section.heading: Notice of Part 13 exemption

content.p: As soon as practicable after making a Part 13 exemption under section 302A, the Minister must:
give a copy of the exemption to:
the person to whom the exemption applies; and
if a different person applied for the exemption under subsection 302C(1)—that person; and
publish a copy of the exemption together with the Minister’s reasons for granting the exemption on the Department’s website.
However, the Minister must not publish under paragraph (1)(b) so much of the exemption or reasons as:
is:
(i) an exempt document under section 47 of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (trade secrets etc.); or

a conditionally exempt document under section 47G of that Act (business documents) to which access would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest for the purposes of subsection 11A(5) of that Act; or
the Minister believes it is in Australia’s national interest not to provide.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.

section.heading: Variation of Part 13 exemption

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, vary a Part 13 exemption:
on the Minister’s initiative; or
on application under section 302H.
Note: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 302N(1).
The variation may vary any one or more of the following:
the specified action;
the provisions from which the action is exempt, but not in a way that results in the action being exempt from additional provisions;
the person to whom the exemption applies;
the period for which the exemption is in force;
the conditions of the exemption, including by imposing additional conditions.
Grounds for variation
The Minister must not vary the exemption as mentioned in paragraph (2)(a), (b) or (c) unless the Minister is satisfied that the exemption as varied is in the national interest.
Note: Subsection 302D(2) applies in relation to determining the national interest.

The Minister must not vary the exemption as mentioned in paragraph (2)(d) unless the Minister is satisfied that the variation is reasonably necessary to address the national interest that is the basis for the exemption as varied.

The Minister must not vary the exemption as mentioned in paragraph (2)(e) unless the Minister is satisfied, in relation to the conditions as varied, of the matters set out in subsection 302E(2), (3), (4), (5) or (6).
When variation comes into force
A variation comes into force on the day specified in the variation (which must not be earlier than the day the variation is made).
Not a legislative instrument
A variation made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Application to vary Part 13 exemption

content.p: The following may apply to the Minister to vary a Part 13 exemption:
(a) the person to whom the exemption applies (the exempt person);
if a different person applied to the Minister for the exemption under subsection 302C(1)—that person, with the agreement in writing of the exempt person.
The application must:
be in writing; and
specify the variation applied for.
Note: For the types of variations that may be made, see subsection 302G(2).
Timeframe for decision
The Minister must decide whether to vary the exemption under section 302G within 20 business days of receiving the application.

Note: If the Minister requests information to make an informed decision under section 302N, days between the request and receipt of the information do not count towards this timeframe (subsection 302N(2)).
Notice if Minister decides not to vary exemption
If the Minister decides not to vary the exemption, the Minister must give the applicant written notice of the Minister’s decision as soon as practicable after the decision is made.
Note: If the Minister varies the exemption, the Minister must give a copy of the variation to the person to whom it applies and the applicant (if a different person) (see section 302J).

section.heading: Notice of variation of Part 13 exemption

content.p: As soon as practicable after varying a Part 13 exemption under section 302G, the Minister must:
give a copy of the variation to:
the person to whom the exemption, as varied, applies; and
if a different person applied for the variation—that person; and
publish a copy of the variation together with the Minister’s reasons for varying the exemption on the Department’s website.
However, the Minister must not publish under paragraph (1)(b) so much of the variation or reasons as:
is:
(i) an exempt document under section 47 of the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (trade secrets etc.); or

a conditionally exempt document under section 47G of that Act (business documents) to which access would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest for the purposes of subsection 11A(5) of that Act; or
the Minister believes it is in Australia’s national interest not to provide.
Note: Subsection 157C(2) applies in relation to determining Australia’s national interest.

section.heading: Revocation of Part 13 exemption

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, revoke a Part 13 exemption, on the Minister’s initiative, if the Minister reasonably believes that:
the exemption is no longer in the national interest; or
a condition of the exemption has been contravened.
Note 1: The Minister may request information to make an informed decision under subsection 302N(1).
Note 2: For paragraph (a), subsection 302D(2) applies in relation to determining the national interest.
Note 3: A Part 13 exemption is taken to be revoked if the Minister decides to accept the surrender of the exemption under section 302M.
A revocation comes into force on the day specified in the revocation (which must not be earlier than the day the revocation is made).
A revocation made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Notice of revocation of Part 13 exemption

content.p: As soon as practicable after revoking a Part 13 exemption under section 302K, the Minister must:
give a copy of the revocation to:
the person to whom the exemption applied immediately before the revocation; and
if a different person applied for the exemption under subsection 302C(1)—that person; and
publish a copy of the revocation together with the Minister’s reasons for revoking the exemption on the Department’s website.

section.heading: Surrender of Part 13 exemption

content.p: A person to whom a Part 13 exemption applies may, in writing, request the Minister to accept the surrender of the exemption.
The Minister must decide whether to accept the surrender within 20 business days of receiving the application.

Note: If the Minister requests information to make an informed decision under section 302N, days between the request and receipt of the information do not count towards this timeframe (subsection 302N(2)).
In deciding whether or not to accept the surrender, the Minister may have regard to any matter the Minister considers relevant.
Notice of decision
As soon as practicable after the decision is made, the Minister must:
give written notice of the decision to:
the person who made the request; and
if a different person applied for the exemption under subsection 302C(1)—that person; and
if the Minister decides to accept the surrender—publish the notice on the Department’s website.
Effect of surrender

If the Minister decides to accept the surrender, the exemption is taken to be revoked with effect from the day specified in the notice (which must not be earlier than the day the notice is published under paragraph (4)(b)).

section.heading: Minister may request further information for making decision

content.p: The Minister may request any of the following persons to provide specified information if the Minister is satisfied that the information is reasonably necessary in order for the Minister to make an informed decision as to whether to grant, vary, revoke, or accept the surrender of, a Part 13 exemption for an action:
the applicant for the decision (if any);
if there is no applicant—the person who proposes to take, is taking or has taken the action;
in any case—the person to whom the exemption applies or is proposed to apply;
any other person the Minister considers appropriate.

If the Minister has requested information under subsection (1) in respect of a decision for which there is an applicant, a day is not to be counted as a business day for the purposes of subsection 302C(3) (application for exemption), 302H(3) (application to vary exemption) or 302M(2) (application to surrender exemption) if it is:
on or after the day the Minister requested the information; and
on or before the day on which the Minister receives the last of the information requested.

section.heading: CITES specimens

content.p: (1) A specimen is a CITES specimen at any time while the specimen is a CITES I specimen, a CITES II specimen or a CITES III specimen.
(2) A specimen is a CITES I specimen if:
the specimen belongs to a species included in Appendix I to CITES; or
a declaration that the specimen is a CITES I specimen is in force under section 303CB.
(3) A specimen is a CITES II specimen if:
the specimen belongs to a species included in Appendix II to CITES; or
a declaration that the specimen is a CITES II specimen is in force under section 303CB.
(4) A specimen is a CITES III specimen if:
the specimen belongs to a species included in Appendix III to CITES; or
a declaration that the specimen is a CITES III specimen is in force under section 303CB.

If an annotation in an Appendix to CITES indicates that only specified kinds of specimens of a species are included in the Appendix, paragraph (2)(a), (3)(a) or (4)(a) (as applicable) refers only to specimens of the specified kinds.

Note: Specimens may be included in an Appendix to CITES subject to restrictions and conditions imposed by or under CITES. These restrictions and conditions are given effect by subsections 303CD(4) and 303CG(3).
(6) For the purposes of this section, assume that the definition of specimen in CITES includes a thing that is a specimen within the meaning of this Act.

a specimen that is not a CITES III specimen because of subsection 303CA(5) is a CITES III specimen; or

section.heading: Discontinuing assessment of a place

content.p: Discontinuance on Council’s recommendation

The Australian Heritage Council may, at any time before an assessment in relation to a place is given to the Minister under section 324JH, recommend to the Minister that the assessment of the place under this Subdivision be discontinued.
A recommendation made under subsection (1) must:
be in writing; and
set out the Council’s reasons for recommending that the assessment of the place be discontinued.
The Minister must consider the recommendation and may, if the Minister considers it appropriate to do so, direct the Council to discontinue the assessment of the place.
If the Minister does not give a direction under subsection (3) within 3 months after being given the Council’s recommendation, the Council must continue with the assessment of the place.
Discontinuance on Minister’s initiative

The Minister may, on the Minister’s own initiative, if the Minister considers it appropriate to do so, direct the Council to discontinue the assessment of a place under this Subdivision at any time before an assessment of the place is given to the Minister under section 324JH.
Further information
In deciding whether to make a direction under this section, the Minister may request the Council to provide any of the following:
any comments received by the Council in response to the notice under subsection 324JG(1) in relation to the place;
any other information relevant to the Minister’s decision that the Minister reasonably believes the Council can provide.

In deciding whether to make a direction, the Minister may request any person to provide any information relevant to the Minister’s decision that the Minister reasonably believes the person can provide.

If the Minister, under this section, directs the Council to discontinue the assessment of a place, the Minister must, as soon as practicable:
give the Council a copy of the direction; and
publish a copy of the direction, and the Minister’s reasons for making it, on the Department’s website.

If the Minister makes a direction under this section in relation to a place, the place is taken to be no longer included in the finalised priority assessment list.

Subdivision A—Directed environmental audits

section.heading: Directed environmental audits

content.p: (1) The CEO may, by notice in writing to a person in the circumstances set out in subsection (2) or (3), require the person to conduct an environmental audit (a directed environmental audit).
Circumstances in which environmental audit may be required
The circumstances are that:
the person:
is the holder of, or is otherwise approved to take an action under, an environmental authority; or
is subject to an environmental order; or
is a person to whom an environmental exemption applies; and
the CEO reasonably suspects that the person has contravened, or is likely to contravene, a condition or requirement of the authority, order or exemption.
The circumstances are that:
the person:
is the holder of, or is otherwise approved to take an action under, an environmental authority; or
is a person to whom an environmental exemption applies; and
the CEO reasonably suspects that:

the action to which the authority or exemption relates has, has had or is likely to have impacts on the matter dealt with by a provision for which the authority authorises the action or from which the exemption exempts the action; and

those impacts are significantly greater than was indicated in the information available to the person who granted the authority or exemption when it was granted or the person who approved a variation (however described) of the authority or exemption when the variation was approved (if any).
Requirements for notice
The notice must specify:
the matters to be covered by the audit; and
the form of the audit report and the kinds of particulars it is to contain; and
the day on or before which the report must be given to the CEO; and
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
Without limiting the matters that may be specified for the purposes of paragraph (4)(a), those matters may include all or any of the following:

an evaluation of the nature of the environment that is or will be affected by the activities, of the person, to which the environmental authority, environmental exemption or environmental order is relevant;
an assessment of the risks to the environment resulting from those activities;
an assessment of the person’s existing capacity, in carrying on those activities, to comply with:
for an environmental authority or environmental exemption—any conditions of the authority or exemption; and
for an environmental order—the order; and
in any case—the requirements of this Act and the regulations;
an assessment of what the person will need to do, or continue to do, in order to comply.

section.heading: Appointment of auditor and conducting an audit

content.p: (1) A person who is given notice under section 458 (the audited person) must:
appoint a person to conduct the audit required by the notice; and
(b) arrange for the person appointed (the auditor) to conduct the audit in accordance with the notice.
Civil penalty: 500 penalty units.
The person appointed to conduct the audit must be:
a registered auditor; or
if no registered auditor is reasonably available to conduct the audit—a person who the CEO has approved for such appointment before the appointment is made.
The CEO may, in writing, approve a person for the purposes of paragraph (2)(b) if:
the person approved is not an officer or employee of the audited person; and
the CEO is satisfied that the person approved has the independence, and the knowledge or experience, necessary to properly conduct the audit.
An appointment of a person to conduct the audit made otherwise than in accordance with subsection (2) has no effect.
An approval under subsection (3) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Nature of directed environmental audit

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person is the auditor for a directed environmental audit; and
in the course of conducting the audit, the person does not deal with a particular matter; and
the matter is specified in the notice under section 458 as a matter that is to be covered by the audit.
Penalty: 30 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is the auditor for a directed environmental audit; and
in the course of conducting the audit, the person conceals, or does not take into account, any information or document; and
the information or document is relevant to the audit.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 6 months.

The auditor for a directed environmental audit may have regard to the results of a previous environmental audit, including such an audit conducted in accordance with a condition or requirement of an environmental authority or environmental order to which the audit relates, if:
the previous audit was completed within the last preceding 2 years; and
the auditor is satisfied that the previous audit is still relevant.

section.heading: Audit reports

content.p: After completing a directed environmental audit, the auditor must prepare, and give to the audited person, a written report that:
sets out the results of the audit; and
is in the form, and contains the particulars, specified for the purposes of paragraph 458(4)(b).
Note: A person may commit an offence if the person provides false or misleading information or documents (see sections 137.1 and 137.2 of the Criminal Code).
The audited person must give the report to the CEO:
on or before the day specified by the CEO under paragraph 458(4)(c); or
on or before such later day as the CEO, on application by the audited person, determines in writing.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is required to give the CEO a report under subsection (2); and
the person fails to comply with the requirement.
Penalty for contravention of this subsection: 50 penalty units.
Subdivision B—Compliance audits

section.heading: Compliance audits

content.p: (1) The CEO may, in writing, require an audit (a compliance audit) to be conducted of activities mentioned in column 1 of an item of the following table in relation to any of the matters mentioned in column 2 of the item.

tr.td: Column 2 Matters to which audit may relate
Activities purportedly covered by an environmental authority
Activities purportedly covered by an environmental exemption
Activities that: (a) are purportedly carried out for the purposes of complying with an environmental order; or (b) are subject to any requirement of an environmental order
Activities purportedly covered by a marine park permission
Activities that: (a) are purportedly carried out for the purposes of complying with a marine park order; or (b) are subject to any requirement of a marine park order
Activities of a kind prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this item
Any matters that: (a) relate to compliance with an environmental law; and (b) are prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this item

content.p: The audit may deal with anything that is:
reasonably necessary for the effective conduct of the audit; or
incidental to any matters to which the audit relates.

section.heading: Single audit or program of audits may be required

content.p: The CEO may require, under section 462, a single audit, or a program of audits, to be conducted in relation to a specified matter or matters included in a specified class of matters.

Note: If the CEO has required a program of audits to be conducted in relation to a matter, the CEO may also require additional audits to be conducted in relation to the matter (see subsection 33(1) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901).

section.heading: Who may conduct compliance audit

content.p: A compliance audit must be conducted by:
an authorised officer; or
a registered auditor.
(2) The person conducting the audit is the auditor for the audit.

section.heading: Relevant person for a compliance audit

content.p: (1) A person is a relevant person for a compliance audit if the person is:
for an audit of activities relating to an environmental authority:
the holder of the authority; or
if the activities are those of a person who is otherwise approved to take an action under the authority—the person carrying on those activities; or
for an audit of activities relating to an environmental exemption—the person to whom the exemption applies; or
for an audit of activities relating to a marine park permission—the holder of the permission; or
for an audit of activities relating to an environmental order or a marine park order—the person who is subject to the order and whose activities the audit is concerned with; or
for an audit of activities mentioned in item 6 of the table in subsection 462(1)—the person who is or was carrying on, or is proposing to carry on, the activities.

(2) A person is also a relevant person for a compliance audit if the person is acting as an agent of the relevant person under subsection (1), and appears to be doing or to have done so in relation to activities to which the audit relates.

section.heading: Conduct of audit

content.p: The CEO need not give notice of a compliance audit.
Before starting to conduct a compliance audit, the auditor for the audit:
must give a description of the scope of the audit to the relevant person for the audit under subsection 462C(1); and

must take reasonable steps to give such a description to any relevant person for the audit under subsection 462C(2) whose assistance the auditor considers will be reasonably necessary for the conduct of the audit (see section 462E).
Regulations may make provision in relation to other matters
The regulations may make provision for and in relation to:
other matters relating to the conduct of a compliance audit; and
the process to be followed after a compliance audit has been completed.
Without limiting subsection (3), the regulations may make provision for and in relation to the following:
information that must be provided to relevant persons for a compliance audit before the audit, during the audit or after the audit is completed;
requirements for reports to be provided in relation to a compliance audit.
Note: A person may commit an offence if the person provides false or misleading information or documents (see sections 137.1 and 137.2 of the Criminal Code).

section.heading: Relevant person must provide assistance

content.p: A person must provide the auditor for a compliance audit with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of the audit if:
the person is a relevant person for the audit under subsection 462C(1); or
the person is a relevant person for the audit under subsection 462C(2) and the auditor requests the assistance of the person.
Without limiting subsection (1), providing assistance that is reasonably necessary includes complying with any request under subsection 462F(1) for the audit.
Subsection (1) does not require a relevant person for the audit to allow the auditor:
to enter premises; or
to take samples of any thing at premises; or
to inspect any thing at premises.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is a relevant person for a compliance audit; and
the person fails to provide the assistance required by subsection (1) in relation to the audit.
Penalty for contravention of this subsection: 30 penalty units.

section.heading: Powers of auditors

content.p: (1) For the purpose of conducting a compliance audit, the auditor for the audit may request a person who the auditor reasonably believes has information or documents that are relevant to the audit to answer questions, provide information in writing or produce the documents.
Note: A person may commit an offence if the person provides false or misleading information or documents (see sections 137.1 and 137.2 of the Criminal Code).
The auditor may make copies of, or take extracts from, a document or record produced under subsection (1).
Subdivision C—Other matters relating to audits

section.heading: Register of auditors

content.p: The CEO must cause a register of auditors to be kept for the purposes of this Act.
The CEO must register an individual in the register if:
the individual has applied for registration in accordance with regulations made for the purposes of subsection (4); and
the CEO is satisfied that it is appropriate to register the individual as an auditor, having regard to:
the individual’s qualifications, knowledge, expertise, competence and independence; and
any other matters as are prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this subparagraph; and
any other matters the CEO considers relevant.
Note: The CEO may impose conditions on an individual’s registration (see section 462J).
If the CEO is not satisfied that it is appropriate to register the individual as an auditor, the CEO must refuse to register the individual.
The regulations may provide for any of the following:
the form and content of the register;
publication of the register;
the form and content of applications for registration and the manner in which applications are to be made;
fees to be paid in connection with registration (including ongoing or recurrent fees to maintain registration);
requirements to be met in order to maintain registration;
review of registration;
suspension of registration in prescribed circumstances;
deregistration in prescribed circumstances;
inspection of the performance of registered auditors in conducting directed environmental audits;
inspection of the performance of registered auditors in conducting compliance audits;
inspection of the performance of registered auditors in conducting environmental audits required by conditions of approvals under Part 9;
other matters in connection with registration in the register.
A fee under paragraph (4)(d) must not be such as to amount to taxation.
The register is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Registered auditors must comply with guidelines

content.p: A registered auditor must comply with guidelines prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this subsection (if any) in relation to the conduct of a directed environmental audit or a compliance audit.
Note: The consequences of a registered auditor failing to comply with the guidelines are set out in regulations made for the purposes of subsection 462G(4).
Regulations prescribing guidelines

(2) Despite subsection 14(2) of the Legislation Act 2003, regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision in relation to a matter by applying, adopting, or incorporating, with or without modification, any matter contained in an instrument or other writing as in force or existing from time to time.
Subsection (2) applies whether or not the instrument or other writing was created for a purpose other than being applied, adopted or incorporated by the regulations.

To the extent that regulations making provision as mentioned in subsection (2) constitutes a subdelegation of the Governor-General’s power to make regulations for the purposes of subsection (1), subsection (2) authorises that subdelegation.

section.heading: Conditions of registration

content.p: The CEO may impose one or more conditions on an individual’s registration as a registered auditor.
Without limiting subsection (1), the CEO may impose conditions setting out the following:
the kinds of audits the individual is able to conduct;
the circumstances in which the individual is able to conduct an audit or a kind of audit;
requirements or restrictions relating to the individual’s independence as a registered auditor.
The regulations may provide for or in relation to any of the following:
the process to be followed in deciding to impose conditions;
notification of such decisions;
review of such decisions;
variation or revocation of conditions;
other matters in connection with conditions.

section.heading: Other audit obligations not affected

content.p: Nothing in this Division affects any obligation of a person to conduct an audit in accordance with a condition or requirement of an environmental authority, environmental exemption, marine park permission, environmental order or marine park order.

section.heading: CEO may issue environment protection orders

content.p: (1) The CEO may issue an order under this section (an environment protection order) if the CEO reasonably believes that:
a person has engaged, is engaging or is likely to engage in conduct consisting of an act or omission that constitutes:
a contravention of a provision of this Act or the regulations; or
a contravention of one or more conditions of an environmental authority under which the person is approved to take an action; or
a contravention of one or more conditions of an environmental exemption which applies to the person; and
the contravention or likely contravention is causing, or poses an imminent risk of, serious damage to a matter covered by subsection (2); and
it is necessary to issue the order for either or both of the following purposes:
ensuring the person’s future compliance with this Act or the regulations, or the conditions of the environmental authority or environmental exemption;
preventing or mitigating the damage caused, or eliminating or reducing the risk of damage posed, by the contravention or likely contravention to the matter covered by subsection (2).
For the purposes of paragraphs (1)(b) and (c), this subsection covers the following matters:
in relation to a contravention or likely contravention of a provision:
for a provision of Part 3—the matter protected by the provision; or
for any other provision—the environment, to the extent that it is dealt with by the provision;
in relation to a contravention or likely contravention of conditions of an environmental authority or environmental exemption:
for an approval under Part 9—the matter protected by any provision of Part 3 for which the approval has effect; or
for a national interest exemption or continuing section 158 exemption from a provision of Part 3—the matter protected by any provision of Part 3 from which an action is exempt under the exemption; or

for a national interest exemption or continuing section 158 exemption from a provision of Chapter 4—the matter protected by any provision of Part 3 that is, or would be but for the exemption, a controlling provision for the action that is exempt under the exemption; or
for a permit issued under Chapter 5—the environment, to the extent that it is dealt with by any provision of that Chapter for which the permit has effect; or

for a Part 13 exemption or continuing section 303A exemption—the environment, to the extent that it is dealt with by any provision of Part 13 or regulations made under Part 13 from which an action is exempt under the exemption.
The order may impose any requirements on the person that the CEO reasonably believes are necessary for the purposes mentioned in paragraph (1)(c), including by doing any or all of the following:
requiring the person to discontinue or not commence specified activities;
requiring the person to change the manner in which the person is carrying on, or is to carry on, specified activities;
otherwise restricting the manner in which the person is carrying on, or is to carry on, specified activities;
requiring the person to take specified action in a specified manner or in specified circumstances.
How order may be issued
An environment protection order may be issued:
by notice in writing; or
if the CEO is satisfied it is necessary to do so because of urgent circumstances—by notice given orally (including by telephone).
For the purposes of subsection (4), the notice may be:

given to the person to whom the order applies, including, if the notice is given orally and the person is not an individual, by giving the notice to any employee or officer of the person acting in that capacity; or
given to any person who is acting as an agent of the person to whom the order applies in relation to activities to which the order relates.

If the order is issued by notice in writing to an agent mentioned in paragraph (5)(b), the CEO must, within 72 hours after the order is issued, give a copy of the notice to the person to whom the order applies.
If the order is issued by notice given orally to a person, the CEO must, within 72 hours after the oral notice is given:
give notice in writing of the order to the person to whom the order applies; and
if the oral notice was given to an agent mentioned in paragraph (5)(b)—give a copy of the notice in writing of the order to the agent.
Other matters
Neither of the following is a legislative instrument:
an environment protection order issued in writing under paragraph (4)(a);
notice of an environment protection order under subsection (7).

section.heading: Content of environment protection orders

content.p: An environment protection order must (subject to subsection (2)):
state the day on which the order is issued; and
state the name of the person the order applies to; and
state the purposes for which the order is issued, including by giving brief details of any alleged contravention or potential contravention to which the order relates; and
set out the requirements imposed on the person by the order; and
specify that, unless extended, or revoked earlier, the order remains in force until the end of:
the period of 14 days after the day it comes into force; or
a specified shorter period.
If an environment protection order is issued by notice given orally under paragraph 474A(4)(b):

a requirement in subsection (1) of this section for the order to contain a matter is taken to be a requirement for the CEO, when issuing the order, to inform the person to whom notice of the order is given of the matter; and
a reference in this Act or the regulations to a matter specified in the order is taken to be a reference to a matter of which the person has been so informed; and
notice of the environment protection order under subsection 474A(7) must include each matter so informed.

section.heading: Supporting documents

content.p: The CEO must, in accordance with this section, provide the person to whom an environment protection order applies with one or more documents that support the CEO’s reasonable belief as to the matters mentioned in paragraph 474A(1)(a).
If the environment protection order is issued by notice in writing, a copy of the documents must accompany:
the notice; and
if the notice was given to an agent mentioned in paragraph 474A(5)(b)—the copy of the notice required by subsection 474A(6) to be given to the person to whom the order applies.
If the environment protection order is issued by notice given orally, a copy of the documents must accompany:
the notice in writing that is required by paragraph 474A(7)(a) to be given to the person to whom the order applies; and
if the oral notice was given to an agent mentioned in paragraph 474A(5)(b)—the copy of the notice in writing that is required by paragraph 474A(7)(b) to be given to the agent.

section.heading: Duration of environment protection orders

content.p: An environment protection order comes into force immediately after notice of the order is given under subsection 474A(4).
Note: For the persons to whom notice may be given under subsection 474A(4), see subsection (5) of that section.
The order remains in force until the end of the period specified in the order for the purposes of paragraph 474B(1)(e), unless:
the order is extended by a variation made under subsection 474D(1); or
the order is revoked earlier under subsection 474D(1).
Note: If extended under subsection 474D(1), the order remains in force for the period as extended, unless revoked earlier (see subsection 474D(1A)).

section.heading: Variation or revocation of environment protection orders

content.p: The CEO may, by written notice given to the person an environment protection order applies to, vary or revoke the order.

The CEO may, under subsection (1), vary the order to extend the period for which it remains in force by a maximum of 14 days. If the CEO does so, the order remains in force for the period as extended, unless revoked earlier.
The period for which an environment protection order remains in force may be extended only once.
The CEO must revoke an environment protection order under subsection (1) if the CEO reasonably believes that the order is no longer necessary for any of the purposes for which it was issued.

section.heading: Person may make representations about steps taken to comply with environment protection orders

content.p: A person to whom an environment protection order applies may make written representations to the CEO about one or more of the following:
steps the person has taken in relation to the purposes of the environment protection order;
steps the person has taken in relation to the requirements set out in the environment protection order;
the reasons why the person considers that the environment protection order should be revoked.
Representations under subsection (1) may be accompanied by supporting information.

section.heading: Person must comply with environment protection order

content.p: Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if:
an environment protection order applies to the person; and
the person does, or fails to do, an act or thing; and
doing, or failing to do, the act or thing results in a contravention of the order.
Penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
an environment protection order applies to the person; and
the person contravenes the order.
Penalty: 300 penalty units.

section.heading: Person must not hinder or obstruct compliance

content.p: A person (the first person) commits an offence if:
an environment protection order applies to another person; and
the first person hinders or obstructs the other person in complying with the order.
Penalty: 300 penalty units.

section.heading: Natural justice hearing rule

content.p: The CEO is not required to observe any requirements of the natural justice hearing rule in relation to the issue or variation of an environment protection order.

section.heading: Giving notice by electronic means

content.p: Paragraphs 9(1)(d) and (2)(d) of the Electronic Transactions Act 1999 do not apply to a notice under this Division.
Note: Paragraphs 9(1)(d) and (2)(d) of the Electronic Transactions Act 1999 deal with the consent of the recipient of information to the information being given by way of electronic communication.

division.heading: Establishment and functions of the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee

section.heading: Establishment

content.p: The Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee is established.
The Minister is to determine in writing the composition of the Committee, including the qualifications of its members.
The Minister is to appoint the members of the Committee on a part-time basis, and must appoint one of the members to chair the Committee.

section.heading: Functions of the Committee

content.p: The functions of the Committee are as follows:
at the request of the Restoration Contributions Holder—to advise the Restoration Contributions Holder in relation to any of the functions or powers of the Restoration Contributions Holder;
at the request of the Minister—to advise the Minister on any matter relating to restoration contribution charge;
at the request of the Minister—to advise the Minister on any matter relating to bioregional plan registration charge or bioregional plan restoration contributions;
at the request of the Minister—to advise the Minister on any matter relating to exemption charge;
any other functions prescribed by the regulations;
to do anything incidental to, or conducive to, the performance of the above functions.
The Minister may give the Committee written guidelines about its functions.

division.heading: Statement of expectations and statement of intent for bodies

section.heading: Application

content.p: This Division applies to the following (each an advisory body):
the Australian Heritage Council;
the Threatened Species Scientific Committee;
the Indigenous Advisory Committee;
the Independent Expert Scientific Committee on Unconventional Gas Development and Large Coal Mining Development;
the Restoration Contributions Advisory Committee;
an advisory committee established under section 511;
any other committee established under this Act.

section.heading: Minister’s statement of expectations

content.p: (1) The Minister may, at any time, prepare and give a written statement (a statement of expectations) to an advisory body that sets out the Minister’s expectations for the advisory body.
In preparing a statement of expectations for an advisory body, the Minister must request advice from the following:
the Secretary;
the advisory body.
A statement of expectations cannot direct an advisory body in the performance or exercise of the advisory body’s functions or powers.
In preparing a statement of expectations for an advisory body, the Minister:
must have regard to any advice requested from the Secretary or the advisory body; and
must have regard to any matters prescribed by the regulations; and
may have regard to any other matter the Minister considers relevant; and
must prepare the statement in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the regulations.
As soon as practicable after giving a statement of expectations to an advisory body, the Minister must arrange for it to be published on the Department’s website.
A statement of expectations for an advisory body replaces any previous statement of expectations for the advisory body.
A statement of expectations is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Statement of intent

content.p: (1) If the Minister gives a statement of expectations to an advisory body under section 510B, the advisory body must prepare and give the Minister a written response (a statement of intent).
In preparing a statement of intent, an advisory body:
must have regard to any matters prescribed by the regulations; and
may have regard to any other matter the advisory body considers relevant; and
must prepare the statement in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the regulations.
An advisory body must publish a statement of intent on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after it is given to the Minister.
A statement of intent is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Part

content.p: National environmental standards are legislative instruments made by the Minister.
Before making a national environmental standard, the Minister must be satisfied that it promotes the objects of this Act and is not inconsistent with relevant international agreements.
A national environmental standard must specify outcomes or objectives. It may also specify parameters, principles, processes or actions for achieving the outcomes or objectives.
When varying or revoking a national environmental standard, the Minister must comply with the no regression principle.

National environmental standards must be applied in making certain decisions under this Act. Those decisions are indicated either by the provision of this Act under which a decision is made or by the regulations. The regulations will prescribe which standards must be applied in making such decisions.
For other decisions, where national environmental standards do not need to be applied, a decision maker can still choose to apply them.

section.heading: Making national environmental standards

content.p: The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make national environmental standards for the purposes of this Act.
Before making a national environmental standard, the Minister must be satisfied that:
the standard would promote the objects of this Act; and
the standard would not be inconsistent with Australia’s obligations under the international agreements specified in subsection 520(3).
The Minister may have regard to any other matter the Minister considers relevant when deciding whether to make a national environmental standard.
A national environmental standard:
must prescribe one or more outcomes or objectives; and
may prescribe any of the following:
parameters within, or principles by which, an outcome or objective is to be achieved;
processes or actions to be followed or taken in achieving an outcome or objective.
A national environmental standard, or an instrument varying or revoking a national environmental standard, may also prescribe:
any matters required or permitted by this Act to be dealt with by national environmental standards; or

other matters (including matters of an application, saving or transitional nature) incidental to matters prescribed as mentioned in subsection (4) or prescribed as mentioned in paragraph (a) of this subsection.

In prescribing matters of an application, saving or transitional nature, a national environmental standard, or an instrument varying or revoking a national environmental standard, may provide that the standard, variation or revocation applies in relation to a decision made on or after the day the standard, variation or revocation commences, regardless of whether the decision relates to an application, referral or other matter made before that day.

section.heading: Incorporation by reference

content.p: (1) Despite subsection 14(2) of the Legislation Act 2003, a national environmental standard may make provision in relation to a matter by applying, adopting or incorporating, with or without modification, any matter contained in an instrument or other writing:
as in force or existing at a particular time; or
as in force or existing from time to time.
The Minister must arrange for a copy of any matter applied, adopted or incorporated to be published on the Department’s website, as soon as practicable after it is applied, adopted or incorporated.
Subsection (2) does not apply in relation to matter that is, or is included in, an Act, a legislative instrument or a notifiable instrument.

section.heading: Varying and revoking national environmental standard

content.p: The Minister may, by legislative instrument, vary or revoke a national environmental standard.
Before varying or revoking a national environmental standard, the Minister must be satisfied that:
the standard as varied, or the revocation, promotes the objects of this Act; and
the standard as varied, or the revocation, is not inconsistent with Australia’s obligations under the international agreements specified in subsection 520(3).
The Minister may have regard to any other matter the Minister considers relevant in deciding whether to vary or revoke a national environmental standard.

section.heading: No regression principle

content.p: Before varying or revoking a national environmental standard, the Minister must be satisfied that the variation or revocation:
does not reduce protections of the environment; and

does not reduce the likelihood that environmental data or information provided to the Minister, Secretary, Department or a Commonwealth agency under this Act or the regulations is appropriate, including as to quality, for the purposes for which it is provided; and
does not reduce the likelihood that appropriate consultation or engagement (including with Indigenous persons) will occur under the Act;
does not reduce the likelihood that outcomes or objectives specified in the standard will be achieved;
meets the prescribed requirements (if any).

In deciding whether the Minister is satisfied for the purposes of subsection (1), the Minister is not required to have regard to the content of any instrument or other writing applied, adopted or incorporated for the purposes of making provision in the national environmental standard in relation to a matter.
In deciding whether the Minister is satisfied for the purposes of subsection (1), the Minister may take into account protections or requirements under any of the following:
this Act or another law of the Commonwealth;
a law of a State or a self-governing Territory;
another national environmental standard in force or proposed to be made.
Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to a variation or revocation of a national environmental standard within 18 months of the standard being made.

section.heading: Consultation

content.p: Before making, varying, or revoking a national environmental standard, the Minister must:
publish a draft of the proposed standard, variation, or revocation on the Department’s website; and
invite public comment on the draft within the period specified in the invitation (which must be at least 20 business days); and
consider any relevant comments made within the specified period.
Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to a variation of a standard if the Minister is satisfied that the variation is of a minor or machinery nature.

section.heading: Consultation in relation to engagement with Indigenous persons

content.p: Before making, varying, or revoking a national environmental standard that relates to engagement with Indigenous persons, the Minister must:

invite the Indigenous Advisory Committee to provide any comments on the proposed standard, variation or revocation, within the period specified in the invitation (which must be a reasonable period); and
consider any comments made by the Committee within the specified period.
To avoid doubt, the Minister is not prevented from making, varying or revoking the standard if no comments are made by the Committee within the specified period.

section.heading: Review of national environmental standards

content.p: The Minister must arrange for a review of a national environmental standard to be started:
within 18 months of the standard commencing; and
at least every 5 years after that.
A standard must be reviewed in accordance with paragraph (1)(a) even if it is varied before the end of the 18 months.

If a standard is varied (other than a variation of a minor or machinery nature) more than 18 months after it commenced, the next review of the standard is to be started within 5 years of the variation commencing.
A review of a standard must consider the extent to which the standard is achieving its outcomes and objectives and what changes, if any, should be made to the standard.
The persons undertaking a review must give the Minister a written report of the review by the end of:
the period of 12 months starting on the day the review commenced; or
if the Minister, in writing, extends that period—the extended period.
The Minister must arrange for the report to be published on the Department’s website as soon as practicable after the report is given to the Minister.

section.heading: Using national environmental standards

content.p: Mandatory use
In making a decision prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this subsection, a person must:
apply any national environmental standard prescribed for the decision; and
apply it in the way prescribed.
Note: Other provisions of this Act may also require a person to apply a standard in a specified way in making a decision (see for example section 136A).
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), the regulations may prescribe the following ways that a national environmental standard is to be applied by a person making a decision:
by the person being satisfied that the decision is not inconsistent with the standard;
by the person being satisfied that the decision is consistent with the standard;
by the person having regard to the standard;
any other way.
Prescribing all or part of a national environmental standard

Regulations prescribing a national environmental standard for the purposes of a provision of this Act that refers to a national environmental standard prescribed for the purposes of the provision may prescribe the whole or a specified part of a standard. If a specified part is prescribed, the provision is taken to refer to the part of the standard that is prescribed.
Discretionary use
A person may, in making a decision under this Act, have regard to any national environmental standard the person considers relevant to the decision.
However, a person is only required to apply a national environmental standard in making a decision under this Act if subsection (1) of this section, or another provision of this Act, requires it.
Effect on validity of decisions

Unless this Act requires a person to apply a national environmental standard in making a decision under this Act, a failure by a person to have regard to or apply a national environmental standard does not affect the validity of the decision.
Insert:

section.heading: Simplified outline of this Part

content.p: The Minister and CEO may publish their opinions on the way in which provisions of environment law should apply in relation to persons, activities and other matters. These are called rulings.

Generally, decision makers are required to act consistently with rulings, but not if they are satisfied it is not appropriate to follow a ruling in particular circumstances. In this case decision makers must publish their reasons.

section.heading: Minister’s rulings

content.p: Ruling about how environment law provision should apply

The Minister may, by written instrument, make for the purposes of the performance of functions and exercise of powers under this Act a ruling setting out the Minister’s opinion on the way in which one or more specified environment law provisions should apply in relation to:
a particular person or a class of persons; or
a particular action or activity, or a class of actions or activities; or
a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, or a class of matters protected by a provision of Part 3; or
a particular application (however described) made under this Act or the regulations, or a class of applications (however described) made under this Act or the regulations; or
particular circumstances; or
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.

The ruling may set out circumstances or factors that, in the Minister’s opinion, are relevant to the exercise of discretion (if applicable) by a decision maker in applying the environment law provision.
(3) A provision of any of the following is an environment law provision:
this Act;
the regulations;
a national environmental standard;
any other instrument made under this Act.
Despite subsection (1), the Minister must not make a ruling in relation to any of the CEO’s environment law provisions (see subsection 514YN(3)).
Ruling about consistency of environment process with national environmental standard

The Minister may, by written instrument, make for the purposes of the performance of functions and exercise of powers under this Act a ruling that sets out the Minister’s opinion on the consistency of a management or authorisation framework, or any component of a management or authorisation framework, with a national environmental standard or part of a national environmental standard.
When ruling takes effect
A ruling takes effect on the day specified in the ruling (which must not be before the day it is published under subsection (7)).
Publication of ruling
If the Minister makes a ruling, the Minister must publish it on the Department’s website as soon as practicable.
Rulings are not legislative instruments
A ruling made under subsection (1) or (5) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: CEO’s rulings

content.p: The CEO may, by written instrument, make for the purposes of the performance of functions and exercise of powers under this Act a ruling setting out the CEO’s opinion on the way in which one or more specified CEO’s environment law provisions should apply in relation to:
a particular person or a class of persons; or
a particular action or activity, or a class of actions or activities; or
a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, or a class of matters protected by a provision of Part 3; or
a particular application (however described) made under this Act or the regulations, or a class of applications (however described) made under this Act or the regulations; or
particular circumstances; or
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
The ruling may set out circumstances or factors that, in the CEO’s opinion, are relevant to the exercise of discretion (if applicable) by a decision maker in applying the environment law provision.
(3) An environment law provision, other than a provision of a national environmental standard, is a CEO’s environment law provision to the extent that the provision:
confers a function or power on the CEO; or
relates to the performance of the CEO’s functions or the exercise of the CEO’s powers under this Act or the regulations.

To avoid doubt, a provision that confers functions or powers on the Minister, or that relates to the performance of such functions or the exercise of such powers, is not covered by subsection (3) regardless of whether the functions or powers may be delegated to the CEO.
A ruling takes effect on the day specified in the ruling (which must not be before the day it is published under subsection (6)).
If the CEO makes a ruling, the CEO must publish it on the NEPA’s website as soon as practicable.
A ruling made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Public consultation before making ruling

content.p: Before the Minister makes a ruling, the Minister must:
publish on the Department’s website:
a draft of the ruling; and
a notice inviting comments on the draft ruling within the period specified in the notice; and
take into account any comments made within the specified period.
Before the CEO makes a ruling, the CEO must:
publish on the NEPA’s website:
a draft of the ruling; and
a notice inviting comments on the draft ruling within the period specified in the notice; and
take into account any comments made within the specified period.

section.heading: Variation of ruling

content.p: Variation of Minister’s ruling
The Minister may, by written instrument, vary a ruling made by the Minister, if the Minister is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so.
If the Minister varies a ruling, the Minister must publish the variation on the Department’s website as soon as practicable.
Variation of CEO’s ruling
The CEO may, by written instrument, vary a ruling made by the CEO, if the CEO is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so.
If the CEO varies a ruling, the CEO must publish the variation on the NEPA’s website as soon as practicable.
When variation takes effect
A variation takes effect on the day specified in the variation (which must not be before the day it is published under subsection (2) or (4), as applicable).
Variation is not a legislative instrument
A variation made under subsection (1) or (3) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Public consultation before variation

content.p: Before the Minister varies a ruling, the Minister must:
publish on the Department’s website:
a draft of the variation; and
a notice inviting comments on the draft variation within the period specified in the notice; and
take into account any comments made within the specified period.
Before the CEO varies a ruling, the CEO must:
publish on the NEPA’s website:
a draft of the variation; and
a notice inviting comments on the draft variation within the period specified in the notice; and
take into account any comments made within the specified period.

section.heading: Revocation of ruling

content.p: Revocation of Minister’s ruling
The Minister may, by written instrument, revoke a ruling made by the Minister, if the Minister is satisfied that the ruling is no longer appropriate.
If the Minister revokes a ruling, the Minister must publish the revocation on the Department’s website as soon as practicable.
Revocation of CEO’s ruling
The CEO may, by written instrument, revoke a ruling made by the CEO, if the CEO is satisfied that the ruling is no longer appropriate.
If the CEO revokes a ruling, the CEO must publish the revocation on the NEPA’s website as soon as practicable.
When revocation takes effect
A revocation takes effect on the day specified in the revocation (which must not be before the day it is published under subsection (2) or (4), as applicable).
Revocation is not a legislative instrument
A revocation made under subsection (1) or (3) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Review of rulings

content.p: (1) If the Minister or CEO (in either case the maker) makes a ruling, the maker must arrange for a review of the ruling to be started:
within 5 years of the ruling taking effect; and
at least every 5 years after that.
A review of a ruling must consider the matters (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
The persons undertaking the review must give the maker a written report of the review by the end of:
the period of 12 months starting on the day the review commenced; or
if the maker, in writing, extends that period—the extended period.
The maker must arrange for the report to be published as soon as practicable on:
if the maker is the Minister—the Department’s website; or
if the maker is the CEO—the NEPA’s website.

section.heading: Using rulings

content.p: In performing a function or exercising a power under this Act or the regulations, a person must not act inconsistently with a ruling that is relevant to the function or power.

Despite subsection (1), a person may act inconsistently if, having regard to the particular circumstances of the matter to which the performance of the function or the exercise of the power relates, the person is satisfied that it would be inappropriate to comply with subsection (1).

If a person acts inconsistently with a ruling because the person is satisfied as mentioned in subsection (2), the person must publish, on the Department’s website (for a Minister’s ruling) or the NEPA’s website (for a CEO’s ruling) a notice setting out:
the function or power; and
that, in performing the function or exercising the power, the person acted inconsistently with a specified ruling; and
the person’s reasons for being satisfied that it would be inappropriate to comply with subsection (1).
